articles.title: Jeremias James: The Argentine footballer who wants to play for Wales
articles.summary: Proud of his Welsh roots, Chile-based Argentine defender Jeremias James hopes for a rule change to help his international ambitions.
articles.body:
There has been a small slice of Wales in Argentina for more than 150 years.

About 160 Welsh emigrants sailed to Patagonia in 1865 to create a new settlement, 'Y Wladfa', where their language, culture and religion could flourish free from English influence and dominance.

The language is still actively spoken there, while more than 50,000 Patagonians can claim Welsh ancestry.

One of those is footballer Jeremias James.

James was born and raised in Trelew, a city founded in 1886 by Welsh settlers in the Chubut province.

Its name translates from Welsh to 'Town of Lewis' in honour of its founder, Lewis Jones.

"I'm part of a Welsh family, a Welsh colony that settled in southern Argentina, specifically in Chubut," James told BBC Sport Wales.

"Five generations of my family were born in Trelew, and I'm part of the the fifth generation.

"Over the years my family settled in Chubut and that's where my story, my family, and all my ancestors come from."

After the first journey across the Atlantic Ocean from Wales to Patagonia in 1865, more followed over the next few years.

Many Welsh immigrants in 19th-Century North America later joined the South American settlement to help sustain the Welsh-speaking community.

After the initial settlement in the Chubut Valley proved difficult, additional groups arrived not only from Wales, but also from established Welsh farming communities in the United States.

"Looking into my family's history, the first member to travel to Patagonia was William James on a ship from the United States," added Jeremias.

"David Stephen James was the first member of the family born in Argentina, and that would be my great-great-grandfather.

"Then came my great-grandfather, my grandfather, my father, and me. All born in Trelew.

"The land in Chubut was granted to Welsh settlers, and my family still live there today. That land belongs to us."

Beyond his Welsh heritage, James has a powerful personal story.

At the age of nine he was diagnosed with leukemia and had to move to Buenos Aires for treatment.

"I was on that treatment for about a year or two until I returned to Trelew, discharged, and gradually resumed my normal life," he said.

After recovering he played for youth teams in Chubut before being scouted by San Lorenzo's academy, joining one of Argentine football's biggest clubs who are based in Buenos Aires.

After making his debut for San Lorenzo in Argentina's Primera Division in 2022, he spent time on loan at Barracas Central, Deportivo Riestra and Alvarado, all based in his home country.

The 25-year-old currently plays for Primera B side Magallanes in Chile, joining them on a permanent basis earlier this year after a successful loan spell.

Even though his family have strong Welsh roots, it is unlikely James will ever be able to play for Wales.

Fifa rules dictate that a player's biological parents or grandparents must have been born in the country they wish to represent.

But even though the current footballing eligibility rules do not work in James' favour, he is eager to find out more about his heritage.

"I was born and raised in Argentina, but obviously I've always been aware of my connection to Wales," said James.

"As you progress and develop in this sport, you always consider the possibility of playing for a national team you have family connections with.

"First of all I would love to visit the country. I haven't had the chance to travel to Wales, and it's something I'd really like to experience to find out more about my roots and where my family comes from.

"It's a dream of mine, and one that I'll surely be able to fulfil someday.

"But of course if the opportunity arises to play in that country, whether for the national team or for a club, it would be something truly very special for me."

A left-footed, ball-playing central defender, James is also strong in the air.

He has been a regular in the Magallanes team this season as they aim to win promotion back to the top flight in Chile.

"I've always been a central defender, and I've always enjoyed playing there," James explained.

"I see my strengths as being a good leader on the pitch and my aerial play.

"We've been lucky in Argentina over the past few years that we've had a very good national team and great defenders.

"I've always admired players like Cristian Romero and Nicolas Otamendi. I've followed their careers closely and tried to emulate what they do on the pitch."

It does not seem likely James will be able to play on the international stage like his heroes.

But rules can change in football, and if that ever happens, it would certainly be welcomed by the Chubut community in Patagonia.

articles.title: Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' football from 1986 World Cup win over England sells for £2.5m
articles.summary: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal in the 1986 World Cup quarter-final victory over England is sold at auction.
articles.body:
The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for £2.5m.

Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England.

After the game, he told reporters it had been scored "a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".

Maradona later scored what became known as the 'goal of the century' in the same game, dribbling past five England outfield players before slotting the ball past Shilton.

Though it sold for $3.3m (£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday, the ball had been expected to fetch nearer $10m (£7.3m).

Speaking to Reuters before the auction, Mike Provenzale, a specialist auctioneer at Heritage, said: "It's a true one-of-one item. Arguably the most significant soccer item that exists."

Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser, who refereed the match in 1986, collected the Adidas Azteca ball at full-time and kept it for more than three decades.

In 2023, he signed a letter to confirm it was the only ball used during the match, which has also been confirmed by further independent authentication.

Bin Nasser sold the ball in 2022 for $2.37m (£1.74m). Its new owner again put it up for auction in 2023 though it did not sell as bids did not meet the minimum value set.

The shirt worn by Maradona during the same match sold for £7.1m at auction in 2022.

articles.title: El preparador de porteros del Lyon intenta agredir a Guendouzi y acaba acorralado en el túnel de vestuarios
articles.standfirst: Pelea al término del partido entre Lyon y Fenerbahce, que terminó con los turcos clasificados para la fase liga de la Champions
articles.summary: Pelea al término del partido entre Lyon y Fenerbahce, que terminó con los turcos clasificados para la fase liga de la Champions
articles.body: La de este miércoles fue una noche para olvidar en Lyon, que vio cómo el Fenerbahce eliminaba al Olympique y se clasificaba para la fase liga de la Champions League. Los goles de Muriqi y Archie Brown pusieron la clasificación muy complicada a los franceses, que pese a descontar por medio de Malick Fofana, no lograron el empate y quedaron eliminados. Después de un partido caliente, el futbolista francés del Fenerbahce Mattéo Guendouzi fue protagonista de un incidente con el preparador de porteros del Lyon, Antonio Ferreira. Guendouzi, con pasado en el Olympique de Marsella, las tuvo con la afición local durante todo el partido. La grada insultó a su familia, según la versión de Guendouzi, y el futbolista no se cortó con gestos hacia los aficionados. Con el pitido final, y cuando Guendouzi se dirigía a una zona donde había aficionados del Fenerbahce, fue asaltado por Antonio Ferreira, preparador de porteros del Lyon. Una mala decisión, porque los compañeros de Guendouzi terminaron golpeándole y arrinconándole contra la entrada del túnel de vestuarios, en unas imágenes que están corriendo en las redes. A Guendouzi le reprendió su actitud su compañero de selección Corentin Tolisso, jugador del Lyon. "Simplemente le dije que fuera a celebrar con su equipo, que mantuviera la humildad en la victoria. Deja en paz a los aficionados del OL, ya están bastante frustrados. Este tipo de cosas me parecen irresponsables. Espero que aprenda de ello", señaló.

articles.title: Northeast's first GM, 17-year-old Mayank Chakraborty and pupil Pratitee Bordoloi become Asia's junior chess champions
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: Mayank Chakraborty became India's 94th Grandmaster and the first from the Northeast region last March. He is still 17. Talking to him, howe.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mayank Chakraborty became India's 94th Grandmaster and the first from the Northeast region last March. He is still 17. Talking to him, however, gives away very little about his age; he sounds more like a man with years of experience on his shoulders.On Tuesday, he added another feather to his cap, lifting the coveted classical title at the Asian Junior Chess Championships in Mumbai. 13-year-old Pratitee Bordoloi clinched the classical title in the girls' category on the very same day.Chakraborty is from Assam. Bordoloi is based out of Bengaluru. However, for the past three-odd months, the distance hasn't mattered much. Chakraborty has been mentoring her, and it found a fairytale moment when both of them walked away champions from the same hall that only hosted Asia's some of the best players under the age of 20."Obviously, I became the champion; that's the best thing that happened to me," Chakraborty told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "But also one of my students managed to become the champion. It increases my happiness."Expanding on their preparation together, he added, "I've been mentoring her for almost three to four months now, and I started it all the way in World Youth in Monte Silvano, Italy."In Italy, Bordoloi clinched silver and became India's only medallist at the 2026 FIDE World Youth Chess Championship. On Tuesday, nevertheless, it was gold, along with a WGM (Women's Grandmaster) norm, which came without much help from her mentor during the tournament."During the tournament, it was a bit difficult because he was also playing, but before the tournament he helped me, specifically in preparing openings," an elated Pratitee told this website.Coming into the tournament as the No. 1 seed, Bordoloi felt the pressure. Her mother, Pranti Dutta Bordoloi, didn't dress it up."If I tell you no pressure, I think it will be totally lie," she said. "Whenever you play as the top seed, automatically, whether you want it or not, you will be under pressure. It's like you're giving someone a one-kilo weight on their head and telling them that they have to run now, and they have to come first."Chakraborty, also the No. 1 seed, had already won the Asian Junior Rapid title once before. But classical, he made clear, is the one that actually counts."Since Classical is the actual main form where you become World Champion, it's like I prove my superiority over everyone else," he added.Further explaining what it means to get his hands on the title, the teenager added, "Rapid Championship ends in one day, and this Classical Championship is a battle for six to seven days. So more hard work, more pressure... Classical chess requires a lot of opening preparation, mental training and all this stuff which Rapid chess doesn't require. Just play. Rapid chess is just about playing."Struggle is still going on. Same struggle, same life.Perhaps life has not changed much since becoming a Grandmaster for Mayank, as he muttered, "Struggle is still going on. Same struggle, same life."However, amid the "struggle", he still finds the room to mentor. How? "Honestly, I'm actually very good at multitasking, so I can manage time. I have a timetable," he said with some palpable confidence. "I have a routine, and I follow it very properly. I don't waste time. I don't have any distractions like social media and et cetera. So I can just focus on my work very well."In the next five days, Chakraborty is scheduled to fly to Turkiye and then Malaysia for chess tournaments abroad. On the other hand, Pratitee and her family are content with the WGM norm and the overall outcome of the Asian Junior C'ships, as her mother concluded, "Honestly speaking, if we do as much as we can in India, it will be very less expensive for us financially."If we do the same thing outside, it will cost 10 times more money for us."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Barça - Athletic: les aguardan con los brazos abiertos
articles.standfirst: Los culés estrenan curso ante su grada contra un rival que no les doble en casa desde hace 25 años
articles.summary: Los culés estrenan curso ante su grada contra un rival que no les doble en casa desde hace 25 años
articles.body: El Barcelona recibe esta noche al Athletic. El Spotify Camp Nou aguarda el cruce con los brazos abiertos. Es el primer encuentro de los de Hansi Flick de la temporada 26-27 ante su grada y lo hace, además, contra un rival con el que tiene grandes registros: es un gran invitado. El Barça no pierde contra el conjunto vasco en LaLiga desde agosto de 2019, los rojiblancos no doblegan a los azulgranas en su estadio desde hace 25 años y fueron el rival del regreso, el curso pasado, al feudo culé en un partido que concluyó en 4-0. Los catalanes afrontan el encuentro, que corresponde a la aplazada primera jornada como consecuencia del descanso de los internacionales, con el objetivo de escalar hasta el pódium de la clasificación. Los azulgranas, que defienden título y que aspiran a conquistar la tercera Liga consecutiva, han arrancado en forma la campaña: se impusieron por cuatro goles a cero al Elche en el Martínez Valero, con doblete de Raphinha y Fermín López y un tanto de Karim Adeyemi, uno de los fichajes de esta temporada. El Barça se cruza hoy con un Athletic con el que no pierde en la LaLiga desde la temporada 19-10, sí que ha caído en la Supercopa de España y en la Copa de Rey, y al que goleó, por cuatro tantos a cero, la campaña pasada, en el partido que supuso el regreso al Spotify Camp Nou tras dos años y medio de exilio obligado por las obras del estadio de Les Corts. Para el encuentro de esta noche, Hansi Flick sigue sin contar con el ansiado refuerzo de un delantero centro, el único objetivo es Julián Álvarez, pero le sobra artillería y gol, como confirmó la plantilla en el encuentro en Elche. Todo apunta a que Raphinha, en un gran estado de forma, volverá a jugar de falso 9, y que las bandas serán para Lamine Yamal y para Karim Adeyemi. Fermín López se moverá, a priori, por la mediapunta, y el doble pivote será para Pedri y Marc Bernal: Gavi es baja por precaución tras el golpe que sufrió en la rodilla contra el Elche. En defensa, tampoco se prevén cambios, y Eric, Christensen, Gerard Martín y Xavi Espart saldrán de inicio contra el bloque rojiblanco. El joven canterano rindió a un gran nivel aunque Joao Cancelo ya va cogiendo la forma física y amenaza su titularidad. Rodri es la gran novedad en la lista de convocados culé. No será titular, pero disfrutará de algunos minutos, según avanzó ayer miércoles Flick. El Athletic, por su parte, hace 25 años que no gana en el Spotify Camp Nou. Sería un gran golpe de Terzic. El nuevo entrenador rojiblanco perdió en el debut frente al Sevilla, en un partido que escoció por los errores en los goles y por el fallo arbitral que acabó con la expulsión de Yuri. La puesta en escena del Athletic de Terzic quedó en suspenso y a la espera de mejores noticias...Al margen del resultado que pueda darse contra el equipo de Flick, que es uno de los entrenadores de referencia de Terzic y uno de los consejeros a los que citó para que le explicase qué supone la Liga, la cita debe ofrecer la sensación de que el Athletic tiene un plan. En el apartado de bajas médicas, Terzic no podrá contar con Vivian y Prados. El central arrastra un problema de aductores, del que se recupera con un tratamiento individualizado que pronto debería devolverle a las rutinas con el grupo, y el centrocampista apareció ayer en el parte médico a causa de “una lesión muscular de carácter leve en el recto anterior de la pierna izquierda”.

articles.title: El Albacete reúne a dos campeones de la Champions
articles.standfirst: La reciente llegada de Munir El Haddadi se une al palmarés de Vallejo en un equipo cada vez más mediático
articles.summary: La reciente llegada de Munir El Haddadi se une al palmarés de Vallejo en un equipo cada vez más mediático
articles.body: El Albacete Balompié puede presumir de algo altamente inusual para un equipo de Segunda división: dos futbolistas con Champions League en su palmarés comparten vestuario en el Carlos Belmonte. La reciente llegada de Munir El Haddadi se suma a la presencia de Jesús Vallejo y confirma el salto de calidad que ha dado el proyecto deportivo que dirigen Toché (en los despachos) y Alberto González (en el verde). Munir levantó la Champions en 2015 con el Barça, en aquel histórico triplete de Luis Enrique culminado en Berlín ante la Juventus. Vallejo, por su parte, acumula dos entorchados en la máxima competición continental, conquistados con el Real Madrid en 2018 y 2022. Entre ambos suman tres títulos de Champions League, algo difícil de ver en Segunda pero que, paradójicamente, esta temporada también encontramos en otro equipo. El conjunto canario cuenta en su plantilla con Jesé Rodríguez, dos veces campeón de Europa con el Real Madrid (2014 y 2016), y con Sandro Ramírez, que también levantó la orejona con el Barça en 2015, coincidiendo en la plantilla con Munir El Haddadi. El dato revela que la Segunda española no se queda atrás en cuanto a calidad y palmarés de unos futbolistas que encuentran en la categoría de plata un destino para seguir brillando. Vallejo y Munir acumulan títulos impensables para la gran mayoría de futbolistas: Ligas, Copas del Rey, Supercopas de España y de Europa, Mundial de Clubes y hasta la Europa League de Munir con el Sevilla. El míster del Alba, Alberto González, destacó la pasada semana en rueda de prensa el perfil humano de ambos, convencido de que su laureado palmarés no les ha endiosado: "Son dos jugadores extremadamente humildes. Muchas veces hasta se olvida que Vallejo ha ganado lo que ha ganado. Munir, que todavía está llegando (al equipo), lo que sé de él, lo que he hablado con otros compañeros que lo han tenido en el vestuario, es que es un compañero espectacular, que sabe estar en el vestuario, que sabe encajar con diferentes perfiles de compañeros, diferentes grupos y que eso no se le va a notar". El técnico malagueño lo tiene claro: "Creo que va a ser fácil trabajar con este perfil de jugadores". La Hypermotion ya no es sólo la antesala de LaLiga, sino también el destino de futbolistas que han sido protagonistas de grandes noches europeas. Y el Alba cuenta con dos de ellos que, tras labrarse un palmarés impresionante con títulos nacionales e internacionales, ahora arriman el hombro con humildad para que en su nueva casa se pueda soñar con más noches mágicas.

articles.title: Kane, a MARCA: "El primer favorito para la Champions es el PSG"
articles.standfirst: MARCA charla con el Bota de Oro europea del Bayern antes del sorteo de hoy
articles.summary: MARCA charla con el Bota de Oro europea del Bayern antes del sorteo de hoy
articles.body: Hoy es el sorteo de la Champions League y MARCA tuvo la oportunidad de indagar la opinión del actual Bota de Oro europeo, un Harry Kane que atendió la pregunta de MARCA en el marco de la Supercopa alemana entre Bayern y Dortmund. Y esto fue lo que dijo el inglés, que da como primer favorito al PSG, actual bicampeón: “Creo que el PSG es el primer favorito, pues la lleva ganando dos años, y luego, por supuesto, hay otros como el Bayern, Arsenal, Real Madrid, Barcelona… Todos los grandes equipos estarán ahí". No obstante, Harry remarca que aún estamos al inicio de todo: "Estamos apenas al comienzo. Estamos al pie de la montaña y hay un trayecto muy largo aún para escalar, muchos partidos por delante, ocho encuentros en la fase Liga y, obviamente, después viene toda la fase de eliminación directa". Harry le da valor a lo que hizo su Bayern la pasada temporada, en la que cayó en semifinales ante el campeón: "Creo que tuvimos una campaña realmente buena en Europa. Perdimos contra un gran equipo como el PSG por un margen muy pequeño, así que a veces tienes que aceptar esas cosas y seguir adelante". La mirada de Harry está puesta ya en esta edición: "Desde el primer día que estoy aquí, sé que también los otros jugadores y los directivos hemos vuelto a trabajar con la misma mentalidad. La temporada pasada ya quedó atrás y veremos qué pasa en ésta. Ahora se trata de seguir avanzando, de luchar por esta temporada y, obviamente, la Champions es uno de nuestros grandes objetivos".

articles.title: Julián Alvarez y sus sueños de verano
articles.standfirst: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.summary: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.body: Situación incómoda, no hay duda. ¿Quién la puso sobre el verde? Julián. En pleno Mundial se despachó, respondiendo a una pregunta intencionada, con que quería cumplir su sueño y que lo mejor sería una transferencia. Algo así. Si a esto le unimos el interés explícito del Barcelona por él y la posterior propuesta al Atlético, denegada tajantemente por Miguel Ángel Gil, acabamos en lo que está sucediendo. El tiempo no ha arreglado nada. Es más, la bola cada vez es más grande. El Atlético firme en su postura de no vender al Barcelona —como también se lo negó al Real Madrid anteriormente—, los atléticos enfadados con el delantero argentino y Simeone haciendo equilibrios para intentar ganar partidos con este asunto en mitad del vestuario. Un despropósito. Y me vuelvo a preguntar: ¿quién puso el problema sobre el verde? Julián. Y me voy al compromiso contractual y no encuentro la palabra sueño. Encuentro cifras, un buen salario y muchos años de compromiso por delante con el Atlético, que lo rescató de un Manchester City donde no jugaba demasiado y donde entiendo que tampoco estaba cumpliendo su sueño, pero no acabo de encontrar en la letra pequeña como causa de resolución de contrato la de no cumplir su sueño. El Atlético tiene unos derechos y unas obligaciones y Julián Alvarez, también. Los contratos están para cumplirse y en caso de desacuerdo hay pactada una fórmula de salida, pero no creo que la fórmula sea la de la presión de las caritas y el malestar. A mí no me gusta que los jugadores se queden por contrato, pero tampoco me gusta que un contrato los proteja tanto en caso de problemas o lesiones y, por otra parte, pretendan saltárselo a la torera cuando los sueños cambian de colores. Aún quedan días de mercado, lo del Barcelona es imposible, no sé si habrá una carambola final hacia la Premier, pero en todo caso no sé cómo Julián Alvarez va a enderezar una situación que torció él y ante la que ahora no puede mirar al tendido y pensar que no ha ocurrido nada. No creo tampoco que sea un tema ni de goles ni de juego. Soñar con unos colores vistiendo otros sí es un problema, y muy serio.

articles.title: Is Bukayo Saka getting back to his best at Arsenal?
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka has struggled to produce his best on a consistent basis in recent months, but could be getting back to top form this season.
articles.body:
Bukayo Saka's performance in Arsenal 's impressive opening-day win has already convinced some fans the Gunners are going to defend their Premier League crown.

The 24-year-old's game-time for the north London outfit was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he picked up in March.

Saka missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

The winger was then taken off during the Champions League final as Arsenal lost to Paris-St Germain in Budapest and his performance was criticised.

England boss Thomas Tuchel also limited his minutes during the World Cup, but asked if he found it frustrating being judged while not 100% fit, Saka said it was a "gamble" he was willing to take.

A rest after the tournament seems to have allowed Saka to start this campaign at his best. He looked sharp against newly promoted Coventry on Friday, giving full-back Jay Dasilva a torrid time while scoring the second goal in the 3-0 win.

The sight of Saka flying down the right wing and involved in a lot of Arsenal 's attacks will be welcomed by supporters.

Because, despite a stop-start season last year, Saka still clocked up 49 appearances for the Gunners and their win percentage was notably more impressive with him in the team.

Did Saka's World Cup play a part in this season's sharpness?

Saka only started three of England's eight games at the World Cup, including scoring a hat-trick in the 6-4 third-place final win over France.

That result secured England's best finish in a World Cup on foreign soil.

Saka, though, had been left out of the semi-final defeat by Argentina, despite starting the last-16 win over Mexico and the quarter-final win over Norway.

The winger said after the victory against Mexico he wished he had been at 100% fitness going into the tournament but accepted "that hasn't been the case".

Saka played just 357 minutes at the World Cup, just 48% of England's total minutes across eight matches at the tournament.

He showed flashes of his quality, providing three assists, which alongside Anthony Gordon was the most of any England player, as well as three goals.

In fact, he registered a goal involvement on average every 60 minutes for the Three Lions during the tournament.

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle

Al-Hilal in advanced talks to sign Arsenal's Martinelli

Saka returned from the World Cup and after a break rejoined the Arsenal squad, playing his first minutes of this season in the Community Shield, coming on when the Gunners were already leading Manchester City 3-0.

His acceleration and sharpness during that cameo was something that was lacking towards the end of last season as the winger looked to help his team get over the line.

And after his starring performance against Coventry in the first Premier League game of the season, he hinted that after low minutes at the World Cup and a summer break he felt back to his best.

"I was training a lot so I could be ready for the start of the season and ready to help the team in the way I know I can," Saka said in the mixed zone after the win.

"It was more about balancing my time off and not having too much of a break. I took seven days off and then started to train again.

"I've put in a lot of work since then and I'm feeling good. I just tried to come back in good shape, so I'm on top of my body."

That motivation seems to have come from the frustration of not achieving England's goal at the World Cup, with the winger returning to training a few days early.

"The World Cup didn't necessarily go how I wanted it to, for myself and for the team as well," he said.

"I felt really hungry after the World Cup, after the season ended. I was looking forward to this new season."

Havertz, Saka, Odegaard and White partnership

Another part of why Saka looks like he is in a flow state so early in the season is the return of Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Ben White to full fitness.

There is no debate that White and Saka's partnership down the right-hand side, with the defender's overlapping runs, unlock the best in Saka.

The partnership he has with Odegaard and Havertz is also crucial to a fluid Arsenal attack and the win over Coventry was just the second time since December 2024 that the trio started a Premier League game together, such have been their injury problems.

There have been questions about whether Arteta is too reliant on Saka, and before the start of this season the winger had played 153 matches, with 61 of them being the full 90 minutes, across the past three seasons.

But with an enforced break through injury and then lower minutes at the World Cup, he could be about to produce the regular scintillating performances we have become used to.

articles.title: Volunteer 'written off' by doctors publishes first book
articles.summary: Jack Marshall shares his story in the book The Boy Who Can't Smile, about his experience growing up.
articles.body:
A man born with a rare condition that means he cannot smile or blink has published his first book, a memoir of his experiences while growing up.

Jack Marshall, 28, wrote The Boy Who Can't Smile after being told when he was a child that he would never amount to anything.

"Doctors said I would never be able to walk or talk," he said. "I was written off by professionals, who couldn't see past my disability."

Marshall, who lives Belton, Lincolnshire, and regularly visits his sister in Stoke-on-Trent for respite breaks, has Moebius Syndrome , a rare neurological condition that has left him with no facial nerves.

He was also born without some of the cerebellum part of his brain, affecting his balance and coordination, is blind in one eye and has reduced hearing.

Having been told by a primary school headteacher that he could only attend part-time, due to being unacademic, Marshall went on to defy the odds.

His mum took him out of his primary and found a place at another school, which suited him much better.

He went on to go to college and university and gained a masters degree in criminology and criminal justice.

"Thankfully, my mum and my sister are very strong women, and have always been my biggest supporters and advocates," he said.

He has subsequently gone on to complete the National Three Peaks challenge and a skydive as well as becoming an active campaigner for disability rights.

In 2019 he was recognised with a British Empire Medal in 2019 for his fundraising.

Marshall now volunteers for Caudwell Children a charity set up by entrepreneur John Caudwell to support disabled and neurodivergent children and their families.

Marshall was supported by the organisation himself and has become a regular volunteer at their Kids' Activities Club in Keele, Staffordshire.

"We were privileged to be able to support Jack, and extremely grateful that he's now giving back to our cause as a brilliant volunteer," said activity programme manager Kayleigh Williamson.

"Jack's memoir is an inspiring story of resilience, family, identity, and what can be achieved, with the right type of support."

"Caudwell Children funded a Strike Force Football Powerchair, which has enabled me to pursue a hobby I really love," Marshall added.

It's opened so many doors for me; I've played competitively, made friends, and I've travelled to new parts of the country."

articles.title: El nuevo coche de Dean Huijsen viene personalizado... hasta en el logo
articles.standfirst: Un G63 AMG de casi 600 CV preparado por Black Label Lifestyle y Urban Automotive es la nueva joya del central blanco
articles.summary: Un G63 AMG de casi 600 CV preparado por Black Label Lifestyle y Urban Automotive es la nueva joya del central blanco
articles.body: Dentro de poco los jugadores del Real Madrid recibirán sus nuevos coches de BMW para la temporada que acaba de comenzar pero algunos de ellos no han esperado a que el patrocinador del club blanco les ofrezca sus opciones... y han hecho sus encargos particulares. Es el caso del central español Dean Huijsen, que acaba de recibir una entrega especial procedente de Londres. Allí, Black Label Lifestyle, una empresa que personaliza coches de lujo, ha estado trabajando en cumplir los deseos del central blanco de transformar a su gusto nada menos que un Mercedes G63 AMG, uno de los coches favoritos de los futbolistas. Se trata de una auténtica bestia capaz tanto de rodar a 220 km/h por una autovía (gracias a su tremendo motor V8 biturbo de 585 CV) como de subir casi por cualquier sitio... que le permitan sus enormes neumáticos con llantas de 20"... en su configuración de serie. En el caso del coche de Huijsen, ha optado por unas de 23" bajo las cuales se esconden pinzas de freno pintadas en Tiffany blue con las iniciales del futbolista... que como se aprecia claramente también ocupa el lugar de la estrella de tres puntas de Mercedes-Benz (además, están bordadas en los reposacabezas) en el frontal.. El central blanco ha sido el encargado de elegir los elementos de personalización. Entre ellos destaca la pintura negra satinada para la carrocería (que le da un aspecto que impone) o el Widetrack Package de Urban Automotive, que es el potencia la agresividad de su look. Se trata de un paquete de 65 piezas que se instalan a mano en un proceso que lleva más de 200 horas de trabajo y que van desde el llamativo capó de fibra de carbono a unas vías ensancahadas en 50 milímetros pasando, por supuesto, por un escape específico con cuatro salidas para potenciar el sonido del V8 de AMG. El precio base del Mercedes G63 AMG en España está en torno a los 220.000 euros, pero una transformación de este calado a buen seguro que ha subido la factura final... notablemente.

articles.title: Oyarzabal no perdió en el Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El capitán de la Real se ganó una ovacion al inicio de partido, junto a Cucurella, por ser campeón del Mundo, y otra cuando fue sustituido, con un 1-1 en ese momento
articles.summary: El capitán de la Real se ganó una ovacion al inicio de partido, junto a Cucurella, por ser campeón del Mundo, y otra cuando fue sustituido, con un 1-1 en ese momento
articles.body: Mikel Oyarzabal vivió contra el Real Madrid una derrota algo menos dura que sus compañeros de la Real Sociedad, porque fue sustituido con 1-1 en el marcado, por un lado, y porque la afición del Santiago Bernabéu le ovacionó al principio del partido y también cuando salió del campo, por haber sido campeón del Mundo con España. El capitán fue titular por primera vez este curso y volvió a evidenciarse su trascendencia para el equipo txuriurdin. Oyarzabal, tras participar en el homenaje a Cucurella por ser campeón del Mundo y agradecer los aplausos del Bernabéu con el pulgar hacia arriba, no tardó en disponer de su primera buena ocasión, un remate cruzado desde dentro del área a los 10 minutos de juego que Courtois despejó a córner. El viernes pasado ya había asistido a Sucic y Óskarsson, en las ocasiones más claras en La Cartuja, y esta vez quería volver a ser tarscendente. Esa ocasión, en vez de provocar que los txuriurdin se crecieran, dio paso a unos minutos de total dominio blanco, lo que llevó a que el capitán se dedicase a defender y tardar mucho en aparecer, buscando cuando lo hizo estirar un poco a su equipo, aunque sin éxito. Pese a ello, insistió en intentar que hubiera mayor protagonismo de los ayer vestidos de negro y en esta ocasión le puso una pelota a Sergio Gómez que con un espectacular voleón se quedó a centímetros de hacer el 0-1. Oyarzabal recibió con decepción el 1-0 del Real Madrid y celebró con alegría el empate de Sucic, antes de un descanso del que volvió al campo para disputar 10 minutos más, los que le aconsejó su cuerpo antes de consensuar su sustitución con Matarazzo, para evitar una lesión al haber realizado muy poco entrenamientos de pretemporada y tener la Real un calendario muy apretado, con hasta cinco partidos en sólo 18 días. De hecho, el 10 de la plantilla realista tendrá que descansar todo lo que pueda este jueves y viernes, porque el sábado ante el Espanyol, partido en cuyos prolegómenos será homenajeado por la Real y su afición, volverá a ser titular, en busca de primer triunfo del curso.

articles.title: Ander Herrera: Why midfielder is playing for free at Real Zaragoza
articles.summary: Ander Herrera has represented some of the world's biggest clubs, but now he is back home playing for free in Spain's third tier - and this is why.
articles.body:
Ander Herrera's most recent competitive game was in front of a raucous La Bombonera crowd playing for Boca Juniors in the Copa Libertadores.

His next will be in the Spanish third division in front of roughly 6,500 fans against a regional side, Gimnastic de Tarragona.

But Herrera says his return to Real Zaragoza on a free transfer from Boca is just as important as any move he has made in his career.

"This is probably the last dream that I wanted to make come true," the Spaniard tells BBC Sport.

"To come back home, to the place where I grew up, that gave me the opportunity to be professional - not only in football, also as a human being.

"And I still have the passion, I still have the desire. I still have that love for football and to do it at home is the best way to end up in my career.

The midfielder has returned to his boyhood club after 15 years away - including two spells at Athletic Club and stints at Manchester United, Paris St-Germain and Boca.

The 37-year-old has won the Europa League, FA Cup and multiple league titles, played under Jose Mourinho, Thomas Tuchel and Marcelo Bielsa, and shared dressing rooms with Lionel Messi, Neymar and Wayne Rooney.

However, success has been in short supply in recent years for Zaragoza, who beat Arsenal in the 1995 Cup Winners' Cup final.

They were relegated from La Liga in 2012-13 - two years after Herrera had left for Bilbao - and after 13 seasons of declining finishes in the second division, fell into the notoriously difficult third tier of Spanish football.

"It has been so sad, of course, for all us Zaragozistas," says Herrera, who watched the club's decline from afar.

"Real Zaragoza belong to Europe, they belong to compete for trophies, to be fighting with the biggest clubs in Spain and in Europe.

"I want to put my quality, my experience and my passion to try to help my team to come back where I think we belong.

"But since the first day I came, I don't want to talk too much about the past. We have been talking too much about what we have done wrong.

"It's always killing our minds why that happened, always thinking about negative things. Let's stop crying about what happened in the past.

"Let's build on the future. Let's come every day to training with a smile."

When Herrera left Zaragoza, who were in financial trouble, in 2011, he knew he wanted to return at some point.

While he did not know what the situation for his comeback would be, he has rejoined the club during their most challenging time - and opted to donate his salary to Zaragoza's foundation.

"I don't need a contract. I have a very successful career. I have taken care of my money," Herrera says.

"I can give this present to myself. To put that shirt on... for free because I wanted to help my club, my team, my city.

"It's something that I wanted to do. It's something that I am able to do and it's something that makes me feel so proud to be able to be here just to help.

"I am not thinking about money or contracts. I feel a privilege to be able to do that."

Herrera was a fervent fan before his promotion to Zaragoza's squad. His idols were from the club and his biggest inspiration - his father Pedro - was also a player before becoming general manager.

Herrera Sr's time working at Zaragoza was when his son's earliest football memories were created, including that famous 1995 European success.

The young Ander watched from home as his team beat Arsenal to clinch the trophy in the Parc des Princes, the home of PSG - a club he later spent three years at.

Herrera says: "You can now see the difference between Arsenal and Real Zaragoza - but we used to fight against those giants."

Herrera's on-pitch peak may be behind him - although he remains focused on short-term objectives such as helping rebuild Zaragoza - but he is sure football will remain part of his future after his playing days are over.

"I like to work with young players," he says. "I like to see the development and the process and I like to help them to avoid some mistakes that I have probably made.

"To help the families also manage situations that I have already managed in the past and I have probably done not as good as I should have done.

"I don't know if I'm going to be a coach of professional football players. I don't close any door because I love football, it's my passion, it's something that I have been doing my whole life and it's something that I love.

"But I don't know in which position I will find my place."

As Herrera's career progressed and he became a senior player in dressing rooms, he saw the effect social media can have on younger players.

"Young players want to run too fast and I think if you make two steps instead of one you can make a mistake," says Herrera.

"When I was in Zaragoza's academy I was one of the best players and I had the opportunity to leave, but I didn't want to leave.

"I have always tried to enjoy every single step that I make in my career and you can see in our academy we are having problems to keep the players.

"But we have stats here that most of the players that leave don't reach professional football and the players that stay have more possibilities to reach it.

"So because you run faster, it doesn't mean you are going to reach the objective faster. Social media is making you run too much.

"Every player has his moment. Just because he's doing it faster than you [it doesn't mean] that he's going to be a better player than you.

"Social media is making us live too fast in every aspect of society."

These are messages that Herrera wants to help pass on to a younger generation, either as a coach or in another role.

But if he does choose to become the former, he has a long, and expanding, list of coaches from the Basque Country to look at for inspiration.

Four current Premier League bosses - Xabi Alonso at Chelsea, Mikel Arteta at Arsenal, Aston Villa's Unai Emery and Liverpool's Andoni Iraola - all come from the northern region in Spain and have had established coaching careers.

Herrera, who was born in Bilbao, adds: "I don't know how to explain it. I think it goes in the DNA.

"The capacity to work, the capacity to respect the sport, to make every step and try to be better every day.

"It's difficult to explain this level of Basque coaches, but I think it is the respect for football that you can see in the Basque Country.

"People will never hear a Basque person saying that something in Madrid is better than in the Basque Country and you can replicate that in football.

"They have so much love for their own things and it's something very special to experience."

But Herrera's future coaching ambitions are on hold.

The club he loves are languishing in the third division of Spanish football - and one thing is on his mind.

"I am so proud and I feel so privileged to do every single step that I have made in my career. Hopefully I can end up successful at home."

articles.title: El Betis, de regreso al bombo de la Champions 21 años después
articles.standfirst: Su única participación fue en la temporada 2005-06 cayendo eliminado en la fase de grupos
articles.summary: Su única participación fue en la temporada 2005-06 cayendo eliminado en la fase de grupos
articles.body: Más de dos décadas después, el nombre del Betis volverá a estar en los bombos del sorteo de la Champions League. El conjunto verdiblanco, como quinto clasificado de la Liga y aprovechando la plaza extra conseguida por España por el rendimiento de sus equipos en las competiciones continentales el pasado curso, conocerá esta tarde sus ocho rivales en la fase de liga del torneo estrella de la UEFA. Un momento histórico en el que el conjunto andaluz regresa entre los mejores equipos del Viejo Continente. En su primera y hasta la fecha única participación en el torneo, después de superar una eliminatoria previa frente al Mónaco, el Betis tuvo que enfrentarse a un grupo durísimo en la liguilla que no logró superar. Liverpool, Anderlecht y Chelsea fueron sus rivales en una primera fases de la competición en la que los heliopolitanos lograron dos triunfos (0-1 ante el Anderlecht y 1-0 frente al Chelsea) y un empate (0-0 a domicilio ante el Liverpool), pero no consiguieron acceder a las eliminatorias. Ahora, con un nuevo formato de competición, se aseguran disputar ocho partidos, cuatro en casa, en La Cartuja, y otros cuatro a domicilio, viéndose las caras con al menos dos de los equipos del bombo donde parten los principales favoritos al título. El equipo de Pellegrini, como de costumbre, tratará de ser competitivo pese a la dificultad del reto, con el sueño de superar esta primera liguilla y disputar por primera vez en su historia los cruces de la Liga de Campeones, lo que supondría un nuevo hito alcanzado por el Ingeniero. Los verdiblancos se enfrentarán a dos rivales de cada uno de los cuatro bombos del sorteo, uno en casa y otro fuera, sin cruces ante equipos españoles en esta primera liguilla en la que hay una clasificación común y donde los ocho primeros acceden automáticamente a los octavos de final, mientras que los equipos que terminen entre el 9º puesto y el 24º juegan un playoff en busca de ese cruce de octavos. Del 25º al 36º quedan eliminados. Ahí está el reto de Pellegrini y su equipo, estar entre los 24 primeros al final de la liguilla. Entre los posibles rivales del Betis, en el primer bombo, están equipos como PSG, Arsenal, Manchester City, Bayern Munich, Liverpool e Inter de Milán. En el segundo bombo puede enfrentarse a Manchester United, Borussia Dortmund, Roma, Aston Villa, Porto, Sporting de Portugal, PSV o Brujas. Del tercer bombo saldrán otros dos de sus rivales entre Feyenoord, Lille, Bodø/Glimt, Nápoles, RB Leipzig, Fenerbahçe, Shakhtar Donetsk y Galatasaray. Y los dos últimos adversarios llegarán del cuarto bombo en el que están Slavia de Praga, Slovan Bratislava, Stuttgart, AEK Atenas, LASK, Como, Lens, Viking, Sabah. Del cuarto bombo, los rivales más complicados, en teoría, son Como, Lens y Stuttgart; mientras que en el tercer bombo, un sorteo benévolo para el Betis sería, en teoría siempre, poder evitar a equipos como Galatasaray, Nápoles y RB Leipzig. Lo que sí está claro por la configuración de los dos primeros bombos es que dos de los grandes clubes europeos visitarán La Cartuja en esta fase y que el equipo de Pellegrini pasará por al menos dos de los estadios de los clubles más importantes del fútbol europeo. Un reto, una aventura enorme, que comienza con el sorteo de esta tarde.

articles.title: Honest Ahanor: Chelsea in talks to sign Atalanta and Italy defender
articles.summary: Chelsea are in talks to sign 18-year-old Atalanta and Italy defender Honest Ahanor for £34.3m.
articles.body:
Chelsea are in talks to sign Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor.

The Blues expressed an interest in the 18-year-old Italian when they signed right-back Marco Palestra from the Serie A side in July.

BBC Sport has been told Atalanta are willing to sell Ahanor if their 40m euro (£34.3m) valuation is met.

Ahanor, who mainly plays at left-back, joined Atalanta from Genoa on a three-year deal last summer for a reported fee of 16m euros, plus 4m euros in add-ons.

He made 28 appearances in Serie A for Atalanta last season, establishing himself as a regular starter for the Italian club. He also made his Champions League debut in a 2-1 win against Club Brugge in September.

In May, he was called up by Italy for friendly matches against Luxembourg and Greece.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has been building his squad since taking over at Stamford Bridge in July, signing England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for a club record £117m , and adding experienced Premier League players Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

Chelsea face Brighton at home in the Premier league on Sunday after beating Fulham 3-2 in their opening match of the season on Monday.

articles.standfirst: El argentino aduce que está indispuesto para trabajar con el grupo. En dos días, partido en el Pizjuán
articles.summary: El argentino aduce que está indispuesto para trabajar con el grupo. En dos días, partido en el Pizjuán
articles.body: No baja revoluciones el culebrón Julián Alvarez. El delantero, por segundo día consecutivo, no se ejercitará con sus compañeros aduciendo una “indisposición” que ya le hizo ser baja en la sesión del miércoles, primera tras el choque del domingo en el que la hinchada del Atlético le mostró su malestar de manera notable. La ausencia de Julián vuelve a centrar todas las miradas del entrenamiento colchonero. Un escenario que, el propio club rojiblanco, reconoce que les está perjudicando y que le convierte en la principal víctima de todo este asunto, como informó ayer MARCA en exclusiva. Con el mercado a escasos seis días de echar el cierre, la aparición del Arsenal es la posible solución a este entuerto. Desde que regresó, Julián había entrenado con normalidad junto a sus compañeros. Fue realizando un trabajo diseñado por el cuerpo técnico hasta llegar a estar listo para jugar unos minutos el pasado domingo ante el Villarreal. Tras los dos días de descanso que concedió el club a todos los futbolistas, la Araña no participó en la sesión de ayer por indisposición. Algo que se ha repetido en la sesión de hoy. La baja de Julián vuelve a evidenciar que la situación que denunciaba el Atlético de Madrid. El cuadro rojiblanco vuelve a ver condicionado su día a día por un caso que ya se alarga en el tiempo mucho más de lo que los rojiblancos hubiesen deseado. La ausencia de la Araña por segundo entrenamiento consecutivo deja al Cholo con pocos efectivos de ataque para preparar el duelo de Sevilla. Y es que en lo deportivo no hay que olvidar que los rojiblancos juegan su próximo partido dentro de apenas dos días. Será el primero a domicilio en un Sánchez-Pizjuán que todavía no sabe si podrá ver a un Julián que no se ha presentado a entrenar por segundo día consecutivo.

articles.body: El centrocampista español Gnangoro Bouare, procedente del Real Betis, se ha convertido este jueves en nuevo jugador del Rayo Vallecano para las próximas cinco temporadas, hasta 2031, según informó el club madrileño. articles.title: Bradley Barcola: Liverpool close in on Paris St-Germain forward in £120m deal
articles.summary: Liverpool are close to agreeing a deal with Paris St-Germain for Bradley Barcola - adding to the doubt surrounding Cody Gakpo's Anfield future.
articles.body:
Liverpool are closing in on the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee that could rise to £120m.

Sources have indicated to BBC Sport that talks have progressed in the last 48 hours and a full agreement is now close for the France forward.

PSG had valued the 23-year-old at £145m but Liverpool are poised to agree a package that will be worth a minimum of £100m and can rise to £120m based on significant individual and team success.

Barcola is right footed but prefers to play on the left wing and his likely arrival adds further doubt around Cody Gakpo's future at Anfield.

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City have shown interest in the Netherlands forward.

Liverpool are also in the market for a right winger, having explored moves for Yankuba Minteh of Brighton and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.

Why Liverpool are ready to make Barcola third £100m signing

What strengths might Barcola bring to Anfield?

The Reds have had offers of £50m and £60m for Gambia winger Minteh rejected by Brighton .

Barcola has become a main target for Liverpool as they look to add potency to their attack following the departures of Luis Diaz and Mohamed Salah in the past two summers.

He moved to PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported £38.5m and has won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, as well as the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

Barcola, who scored three goals for France in this summer's World Cup, can also play on the right or through the middle and could provide cover for Alexander Isak as Hugo Ekitike recovers from a serious Achilles injury.

articles.body: La UEFA debe anunciar este mes de septiembre la sede de la final de la Champions de 2029. Si la final de 2027 será en El Metropolitano, el Camp Nou tiene muchas opciones de ser la elegida para el 2029. El otro aspirante es Wembley, pero todo apunta a que las preferencias de la UEFA apuntan más a Barcelona. Uno de los principales motivos es el aforo, ya que los 105.000 espectadores facilita mucho el reparto de entradas y cumplir las aspiraciones de los clubes, que siempre reclaman más localidades de las que se les puede ofrecer ante la enorme demanda de sus aficionados. la ciudad de Barcelona es otro aliciente más y el hecho de que hace ya tiempo que no es la elegida mientras que el Madrid ganó la decimoquinta en 2024 en Londres, sin olvidar las finales de 2011 que se llevó el Barçá ante el United y la de 2013. El Camp Nou no ha sido aún sede de la final en este siglo XXI. La primera fue en 1989, con triunfo del Milan ante el Steaua (4-0) y la de 1999, con la famosa remontada del United al Bayern en el descuento. El Barça ha vuelto además a la UEFA tras el proyecto fallido de la Superliga y las relaciones entre Joan Laporta y Aleksander Ceferin han recobrado la normalidad.

articles.title: Esther Gonzalez: Gay World Cup star's move to Saudi Arabian club attracts fan backlash
articles.summary: Spain forward Esther Gonzalez attracts backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
articles.body:
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.

The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.

Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".

However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.

Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.

Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.

According to Spanish outlet El Mundo, , external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.

Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.

The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.

The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.

Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.

Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.

BBC Sport has contacted Gotham FC for comment.

articles.title: Leicester: Russell Martin aims to halt slide down the leagues
articles.summary: Manager Russell Martin is trying to end his own miserable period of results as he attempts to stop Leicester's downward spiral.
articles.body:
A draw and a defeat to start their League One season. One victory in 11 league matches. A player exodus. A new manager already under pressure. And the club up for sale.

These are, to put it mildly, not happy times for anyone connected with Leicester City.

The club are in a very different place than they were a decade ago, when they were basking in the joy of being the Premier League's most unlikely champions.

Celebrations marking that 10-year anniversary throughout the year are unlikely to offer supporters much respite. The reminder of those glory days might even pour more salt in the wounds.

Soon after the Foxes were relegated from the Championship, King Power Stadium hosted a 10-year anniversary match which was billed as the 5,000-1 celebration - their initial odds for winning the league in 2015-16.

Players from that Foxes squad faced an All Star XI managed by Tony Pulis and in scorching conditions in front of about 5,000 fans, it finished 0-0.

Sixteen days later, Russell Martin was appointed manager. He joins with his reputation under the spotlight as he faces the task of turning around the Foxes' downward spiral to the third tier for the first time since 2009.

Since May 2024, when he led Southampton to the Premier League through the play-offs, Martin has won just two league games in charge of Saints and Rangers, whom he managed for just 123 days.

Leicester have started the league season with a draw at Notts County and a 2-1 defeat at home to Burton Albion.

That result led to a number of bets being placed on the club to drop even further - into League Two. Their odds of a third successive relegation are now 33-1.

Leicester's alarming start to the season is amid a backdrop of uncertainty off the field, with Thai owners King Power seeking to sell the club after 16 years in charge.

An eight-page sales booklet has been produced to help attract potential buyers, but no official announcement about the sale has come from the Srivaddhanaprabha family, who run King Power.

Concerns about Leicester's ownership have grown since 2022, when they invested heavily in the transfer market but then failed to qualify for European football.

The Foxes' accounts revealed they lost nearly £100m in both 2021-22 and 2022-23, resulting in a six-point deduction for breaches in profit and sustainability regulations in 2025-26.

Leicester finished last season in 23rd place in the Championship, five points adrift of safety.

Martin was given a three-year contract when he joined in June and while the personnel in the squad will change before the transfer window closes, the first four competitive games of the season have brought doubts about the suitability of his style.

"He was not a popular choice with the fans," says Lynn Wyeth, a member of the Foxes Trust.

"We're not particularly enamoured with the 'tippy tappy' passing football. That doesn't work if you've got players who can't do it, and you put yourselves under pressure at the back.

"But maybe he'll get his new boys being able to play how he wants them to."

Funds have been generated this summer with the sales of Abdul Fatawu to Ipswich Town and 17-year-old Jeremy Monga to Manchester City.

However highly paid players remain from Leicester's Premier League days, with the former Tottenham midfielder Oliver Skipp sent off against Burton.

The latest signing is 19-year-old Finnish defender Ilari Kangasniemi, a ball-playing six foot six inch centre-back who many in his home country hope will develop into the next Sami Hyypia.

Playing out from the back is a key part of Martin's philosophy and Leicester had 73% overall possession in the defeat to Burton.

On Saturday they travel to face MK Dons, where Martin began his managerial career and where his reputation for patient, possession-oriented football was first established.

Foxes fans are used to seeing that kind of style - with mixed results - having watched teams managed by Brendan Rodgers, Enzo Maresca and Marti Cifuentes in recent years.

"I worry that it's a team that doesn't look as if it's got enough fight in it for a League One battle," Phil Holloway, of Leicester Fan TV, told the BBC Leicester podcast, When You're Smiling.

"I'm not here calling for Russell Martin out, although a lot of fans have already done that. I just feel like we want to change the style of football as a fanbase. But it's not going to happen under Russell Martin."

Martin's time at Rangers marked a particularly low point in the 40-year-old's management journey. Their only Scottish Premiership victory was thanks to an added-time winner against Livingston. He was sacked in October 2025.

There were, though, signs of progress for Leicester in their 3-1 defeat to Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup. After testing Premier League opposition, Martin felt his squad was turning a corner.

"The team is so young," he told BBC Radio Leicester.

"We haven't been together very long. We've signed a lot of players, there's been a lot of change. The energy at this club has been really difficult for two years - that takes a lot of energy to shift that energy round."

It is 17 years since Leicester City last played in the third tier of English football. At times, that period has felt like the most precipitous football rollercoaster.

Promotion to the Championship in 2009 was followed by defeat to Watford in the 2013 play-off semi-finals, a game made famous for a late winner scored by Troy Deeney.

Leicester reached the Premier League the following season, famously survived relegation and then won the title.

Anniversary celebrations for the 2015-16 Premier League champions continue into October but that exhilarating summer now feels like a distant memory.

The decade that has followed has included a Champions League quarter-final, an FA Cup win, one promotion from the Championship and three relegations.

In the latest chapter in the story of their post-title win, Leicester fans will hope the early season problems are the result of a young squad adjusting to new methods, rather than a sign their club could fall even further.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola to Liverpool: PSG and France forward is quick, strong, versatile, intelligent – and in demand this summer
articles.summary: Is Bradley Barcola a good signing for Liverpool with him on the brink of a Premier League move? Having spoken to the Paris Saint-Germain forward's old academy boss, Adam Bate examines the strengths and weaknesses of the France international to find out more…
articles.body:
The 23-year-old France international has just won the Champions League with PSG back-to-back but had to be content with coming off the bench in both finals. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's arrival from Napoli in January of 2025 established him as first choice on the left.

But just because Barcola is not a guaranteed starter in Paris does not mean that he is not a guaranteed star. This is a player with pace, physicality and intelligence, someone whose skills have been honed under Luis Enrique. With Barcola, the potential is as vast as the fee.

For a player so highly rated, Barcola's rise has been serendipitous. At Lyon, he was on the fringes of the first team under France legend Laurent Blanc until a player exit changed everything. "That was a turning point," Jean-Francois Vulliez told Sky Sports .

"A club in Switzerland was interested because he was not playing for the first team. At that time, Blanc was the coach and we had Karl Toko Ekambi. But he decided he wanted to leave so the coach decided to stop the loan because we might need Bradley.

Vulliez explained: "It was a key moment because he realised that if Toko Ekambi left, Bradley could be a solution and there was an opportunity to use him. Toko Ekambi did leave. Bradley stayed. One match later, there was an injury and Laurent needed him."

Having worked with Barcola as a boy in Lyon's academy, Vulliez knows him well. In fact, he actually followed Barcola to PSG and now works as a development coach for the French and European champions. In his job, he has seen plenty of standout youngsters.

But Barcola was not necessarily one of them. He was a talent, for sure. But this level of success? That was not obvious. "He was a normal kid, he never played above his age category, never jumped a stage. His maturation was a normal process," he explained.

"It is an interesting pathway because every player is different. Sometimes, there are players like [Kylian] Mbappe who mature very early. Others need time. Bradley never played for France's age-group teams. He was a good player but not physically ready.

"We were very patient with him at Lyon because we knew he had the skills, we just had to wait for that maturation process, that psychological maturation, that physical maturation. When that transformation eventually happens, they will improve quickly."

Following Toko Ekambi's exit, Barcola scored five goals in nine games in early 2023 and after impressing for his country at that summer's European Under-21 Championship, there came a protracted move to PSG. "His body was in Lyon but his head was in Paris."

The three seasons that have followed have brought 13 trophies and 39 goals in over 150 appearances. Under Luis Enrique, he has adapted his game, taking much better care of the ball than before. Barcola knows when to run at defences and when to keep it simple.

The player that Barcola is today is a product of that understated youth career. A late developer physically, dominating defenders was not an option as a teenager. That forced him into finding other ways. "He developed his intelligence," pointed out Vulliez.

"He was able to scan the pitch, take good information and use the space. Very early, he had this and he had speed. Then, he progressed with his muscles, became powerful. It is a combination of these tactical abilities, technical abilities and physical abilities."

Barcola has been used primarily as a left-sided wide forward at PSG. But his instincts are closer to that of a striker than a winger. Indeed, he played up front at Lyon until the age of 17. From that flank, he can cut inside and shoot into the far corner with his stronger foot.

They are instincts that are hard to teach and top clubs cherish those in wide positions who possess them because it is not enough to look good - players need numbers. Barcola is balanced, in this sense, because he can score goals and create chances for others.

This graphic highlights his impressive shot volume for PSG, ranking among the top 10 players in Ligue 1 per 90 minutes last season. Playing wide does not stop him. "He is very clever with his runs inside." The timing of those movements is an important trait.

"Because he played as a striker, he retains that ability to know when he needs to come inside and when he needs to run beyond. With Bradley in your team, you need to use this capacity to come between the lines or run from deep, because it is his strength.

"We never had a problem with him at the academy because he is intelligent and listens so when you are the coach that makes it easier to manage him because he can adapt to whatever strategy the coach wants to use. He understands because he is clever.

"I do not think you can transform a player after the age of 17 because if the player does not have the intelligence at that age then they will never have it. That is why it is vital to develop this intelligence early. Bradley has it. You can adapt his position later."

More will be demanded as he progresses. His finishing can be a little lax. Enrique has pushed him to become more clinical. But there is time. "There are many very good players who improved their finishing when they became more mature," said Vulliez.

"As with every young player, sometimes they need that push but he has the mind to do it and that makes it easier. Maybe the left wing is the better position for him right now but I am curious to see how he develops because I believe he is able to become a No 9."

That flexibility makes him appealing. Barcola has operated on the right too and has the pace to get to the byline if that is what the coach wants from him. He ranked among the top 10 fastest players in the Champions League last season. He can play knock and run.

He is a better player than the one who arrived in Paris, better too than the prospect in Lyon's academy. "Nobody could have imagined this," Vulliez conceded. The question now being asked by clubs regarding Barcola is how much better he could still become.

articles.title: Liam Delap signs for Nottingham Forest: From Harry Kane's successor to Chelsea outcast – can he thrive at new club?
articles.summary: BBC Sport examines what went wrong for Liam Delap at Chelsea and how he could bounce back in new surroundings.
articles.body:
Liam Delap has completed a club record £50m transfer to Nottingham Forest from Chelsea .

The striker has signed a five-year deal at the City Ground after just a year at Stamford Bridge.

"This is a massive club with a big history," Delap said.

"I spoke to the manager (Oliver Glasner) and I like his way, I think he can be the one to really help me develop and make that next step and hopefully I can bring goals here.

"As a team we can build something really strong and the main aim is to challenge and be a top club in the Premier League."

In a summer of staggering transfer fees, the move stands out.

An outlay of £50m for a striker who scored one league goal last season – at a £20m profit to Chelsea – has caught the eye.

But Delap is only 23 and has scored goals in the Premier League before.

BBC Sport examines whether a move to Forest can reignite the career of a young player hoping to marry progress with his undoubted potential.

The finest season of Delap's career to date was undoubtedly his first of regular football at the highest level.

When Ipswich paid an initial £15m for his services from Manchester City in July 2024, it appeared sensible business – a below market value fee for a promising England Under-21 international with the capacity to improve quickly.

The faith of then Ipswich boss Kieran McKenna was repaid in spades when Delap scored 12 goals in his first Premier League campaign in 2024-25 despite operating in a side that would win four games all season and go on to be relegated in 19th place.

Key to his success at Portman Road was a manager who played to Delap's strengths of power, physicality and ability to carry the ball at pace.

He made 26 shot-ending carries that season – the most of any striker in the Premier League.

A burst of six goals and one assist in the first 12 games of that campaign saw Delap earn widespread acclaim from former players.

On Match of the Day in November 2024, former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy said: "I would probably go as far as to say he is the obvious long-term successor to [Harry] Kane. I think he is the best young English striker out there.

"I just don't see a weakness for him. He has scored enough goals in a struggling side really, but if he gets a lot of chances he will score more.

"He has just got that lovely balance between physical and technical [ability] and rarely do you get both. He is a super talent."

"Can Liam play for the biggest clubs in the country, the biggest clubs in the world? He certainly can. I fully believe that." The words of McKenna when Delap began to be linked with a raft of top-flight teams towards the end of 2024-25.

The son of former Derby County defender Rory ultimately opted for Stamford Bridge.

The decision to join a congested Chelsea squad as a still-raw talent was met with some scepticism but the attraction of reuniting with then Blues head coach Enzo Maresca may have been a decisive factor.

Maresca was Manchester City 's under-21 boss when Delap enjoyed great success with the club's academy, scoring 24 goals in 20 matches in 2020-21 as City won the Premier League 2 title.

His move to Chelsea did not work out. It began with Delap's decision to rule himself out of last summer's Under-21 European Championship - a tournament that England would go on to win – to make himself available for Chelsea 's Club World Cup campaign.

The former Stoke, Preston and Hull striker then scored just three goals in 47 appearances, a loss of form which resulted in Chelsea giving Delap's number nine shirt to Joao Pedro before his departure was sanctioned this summer.

Delap's struggles at Chelsea have been underpinned by three managerial changes and hamstring and shoulder injuries, but also difficulties adjusting to a different gameplan.

Whereas Ipswich used Delap's speed effectively by counter-attacking into space behind high defensive lines, Chelsea focused more on building possession.

In 2025-26, Chelsea totalled 123 build-up attacks and 613 sequences of 10 passes or more. In 2024-25, Ipswich's respective numbers were 57 and 247.

As a result, the capacity for Delap to carry the ball at pace into space and shoot – arguably his unique selling point as a player – was dramatically reduced. He made just six shot-ending carries for Chelsea in the Premier League, having amassed 26 for Ipswich and 38 in the previous season with Hull in the Championship.

Shorn of confidence and lacking minutes, Delap was still culpable for failing to take chances last season.

At Ipswich, his shot conversion rate was a career-best 17.7%, scoring 12 goals from an expected goals tally of only 9.3. At Chelsea , his shot conversion rate dropped to just 2.8%, scoring only once in the league from an xG of 4.5.

Confidence aside, part of the puzzle still to be solved with Delap is how best to utilise his impressive strength without his penchant for the physical element of Premier League football becoming counter productive.

Unnecessary tangles with defenders are so often a hallmark of Delap's do-or-die approach, even when playing his best football.

He competed in 413 duels in 2024-25, ranking him third of all Premier League players aged under 23, but only won 157 of them - suggesting he has the tendency to chase lost causes.

Additionally, he committed the second-most fouls of any player (72) and ranked joint second overall for bookings, matching 12 goals with 12 yellows cards that season.

The overriding positive for Forest fans digesting Delap's inflated fee – which can be partly explained by Ipswich reportedly receiving 20% of any profit made on their £30m sale to Chelsea last summer – is that manager Oliver Glasner's man-management and tactical set-up are both likely to suit the new arrival.

Glasner tends to prefer playing without the ball – his Crystal Palace team averaged 46% possession last season – while the Austrian also likes to attack directly at pace, suiting Delap's natural assets.

Glasner also has recent form for turning around a centre-forward's career after transforming Jean-Philippe Mateta at Palace.

Mateta improved his shot conversion rate and halved the number of minutes it took to score goals under Glasner, operating in the same type of target-man role that Delap is set to fulfill at Forest

Delap also remains a valuable commodity in the sense he is one of only 10 English forwards aged 23 or under playing regularly in Europe's top five leagues.

Once heralded as Kane's successor, international ambitions may have to wait for the time being.

But Glasner improved Mateta to the point of playing at the World Cup earlier this summer with France.

Significant interest will surround how far he can take Delap.

articles.title: El Benfica pujará por Josema Giménez hasta el final del mercado
articles.standfirst: Se abren posibilidades para el central del Atlético antes del martes próximo
articles.summary: Se abren posibilidades para el central del Atlético antes del martes próximo
articles.body: Josema Giménez tiene el mercado abierto hasta el próximo martes para ver si juega en otro club esta temporada o sigue en el Atlético, algo no descartable si no llega un equipo top que satisfaga a las tres partes. Según ha podido saber MARCA, las noticias que llegan desde Portugal hablan de un fuerte interés del Benfica por contar con un futbolista que, a sus 31 años y con 12 de experiencia en el Atlético, está en disposición de rendir a la perfección en un club de nivel de Europa. Así las cosas, el Benfica pujará hasta última hora del mercado por hacerse con sus servicios. El club lisboeta, que ha sufrido la marcha de Otamendi a River, quiere recuperar el trono portugués tras la marcha de José Mourinho al Madrid y la llegada de Marco Silva. No es el único equipo que se ha interesado por él. Josema tiene un buen cartel en Europa, y sólo dejaría el club de sus amores en Madrid para unirse a un proyecto ganador y con opciones de todo. Se deben dar, eso sí, las condiciones de pago de la ficha del futbolista y que la cesión cumpla las expectativas de Josema y del Atlético, que podría vivir sin el uruguayo esta temporada, pero que nunca va a regalar a uno de sus principales activos dentro del vestuario.
