articles.title: “La afición del Atlético tiene más memoria que cuatro goles”
articles.standfirst: Javi Lázaro debate en La Tribu la situación de Julián Álvarez en el equipo rojiblanco y avisa del futuro
articles.summary: Javi Lázaro debate en La Tribu la situación de Julián Álvarez en el equipo rojiblanco y avisa del futuro
articles.body: Pedro Riesco, Amalio Moratalla, Nacho Labarga, Javi Lázaro y Diego Picó han sido los tertulianos de este jueves en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por la victoria del Real Madrid y el tema de Julián Álvarez. Una de las opiniones más contundentes sobre la situación del argentino fue la de Pedro Riesco, apuntando a que lo sucedido supone "una última vuelta de tuerca" en una situación muy complicada. "El Atlético de Madrid se ha mostrado inflexible en privado y en público. Creo que Julián Álvarez debería saber que no va a ir al Barcelona. Si va a salir del Atlético de Madrid, va a salir al Arsenal", señaló durante el debate. El papel del Barcelona generó uno de los intercambios más intensos entre los tertulianos. Nacho Labarga defendió que lo ocurrido forma parte de las prácticas habituales del mercado: "No es raro estar hablando con un futbolista que tiene contrato", poniendo como ejemplo que "el otro día Mourinho dijo tranquilamente en una entrevista que había hablado con Rodri". La réplica fue inmediata por parte de Ainhoa Sánchez: "El Barcelona no ha respetado al Atlético de Madrid". Amalio Moratalla recordó que el Atlético "ha iniciado un proceso legal sobre esta manera de proceder del Barça" y que todavía se desconoce cómo terminará. Javi Amaro quiso separar el contacto con un futbolista de lo que considera que ha ocurrido en este caso: "Una cosa es hablar y otra generar este clima de tensión". "Eso es lo que ha denunciado el Atlético de Madrid", diferenció antes de añadir que el club considera que "se han superado unas barreras de falta de respeto". La gestión del propio Julián tampoco quedó al margen de las críticas. Amalio Moratalla calificó como "muy feas" sus declaraciones sobre sus sueños: "Te vistes una camiseta en la que sueñas y sueñas con otra. Complicado, ¿eh?". Otro de los participantes resumió su actuación asegurando que "se equivocó" y que siguió "una hoja de ruta errónea". Sobre qué pretende hacer ahora el Atlético, el presentador de La Tribu fue clara: "El Atlético de Madrid tiene claro lo que tiene que hacer, lo que quiere hacer". Y, sobre todo, apareció una línea roja: "No se lo va a vender a Barcelona, eso está claro. El Atlético de Madrid lo traspasa por 150 millones a quien lo quiera, menos a Madrid o a Barcelona". El debate terminó mirando también a un escenario en el que Julián permanezca en el Metropolitano tras el cierre del mercado. "Claro que van a poner a Julián a jugar", se aseguró. Javi Lázaro advirtió de que recuperar completamente a la grada podría ser mucho más complicado: "Yo creo que el Atlético de Madrid tiene más memoria que cuatro goles". Amaro también se defendió que la firmeza del Atlético responde a una cuestión que va más allá del dinero: "Por primera vez en mucho tiempo el Atlético de Madrid se siente orgulloso de una decisión de club". Una postura que deja el futuro de Julián Álvarez abierto a pocos días del cierre del mercado.

articles.title: At USC, Hollywood's spotlight finds you. Jayden Maiava is ready for it
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava has flown under the radar at USC, but a Heisman Trophy-worthy season is needed for the Trojans – one he's ready for.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – Jayden Maiava finds it hard to believe where he's at.

That's not something you'd expect from the Southern Cal starting quarterback, a spot that has always leaned into LA's glitz and glamour, with Carson Palmer , Matt Leinart and Caleb Williams proof they never shy away from the Hollywood spotlight.

This is a kid from Pālolo, a neighborhood near Honolulu, just a mile away from the famed Diamond Head crater. To most, living on the island sounds like paradise, especially when he had all seven siblings, uncles and aunts in the area to be with, but it was anything but for Maiava.

"It was a rough neighborhood. Definitely a neighborhood I wouldn't want my own kids to live in," Maiava told USA TODAY Sports. "We faced a lot of adversity, a lot of ups and downs."

Football wasn't something he viewed as a possible career. To Maiava, and plenty of other kids, it was just something to get out of the house and avoid trouble.

So you can imagine as he sits inside USC's brand new $225 million, 163,000 square-foot football facility as the man at the center of a college football blue-blood, it's tough to grasp this reality — especially when your team needs the whole country to know who you are.

The 2026 season is a pivotal one for the Trojans , and it can all hang on Maiava in taking the team to its first College Football Playoff appearance.

This is his third season in the program, but he has mostly flown under the radar. Not just unusual for a USC quarterback, but odd considering his coach Lincoln Riley is known for having undeniable signal-callers. He doesn't command that much attention, and for a guy as humble as Maiava, that's perfectly fine.

But pretty soon, you won't be able to ignore him much longer.

"If you're not paying attention to him, then you just don't know a ton about college ball," Riley told USA TODAY Sports in May. "He keeps playing like he's capable of, he won't give people a choice."

A low-key profile might be because Maiava wasn't a heralded quarterback out of high school. Whether it was at UNLV or USC, he began as a backup. He only found the field because of injury at UNLV in 2023. USC made the switch in 2024 after inconsistency from Miller Moss .

In each instance, Maiava proved he should have been starting in the first place. He led UNLV to the Mountain West championship game, and after his transfer to the Trojans didn't generate much noise, he stepped in for a 4-5 team and won three of the last four.

The 2025 campaign was the first time in Maiava's college career he was the guy from the jump. He threw for 3,711 yards — fourth-most in FBS — with 24 touchdowns and an additional six scores on the ground. He led the country with a 91.2 quarterback rating, even better than Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza.

When he's gotten the chance, Maiava has delivered, but becoming one of the best quarterbacks was not something many saw coming. Luckily, the guru in Riley gave him a piece of advice that stuck with him, helping him blossom and remain confident: "Decisiveness always wins."

"You don't want to play the position hesitant," Maiava said. "Coach Riley's the best coach in college football, so it's hard to mess up. When you go out there, just continue to trust it and play fast and continue to trust on routine plays."

Even with the rising star status, that humility remained. Over the summer, EA Sports reached out about him being one of the athletes on the cover of College Football 27 . Just about anyone would immediately jump at the opportunity, but that wasn't necessarily the case with Maiava.

Because again, he found it hard to believe.

"I'd rather have somebody else's face up there," Maiava said. "I can just think of so many other players that it's so deserving for them, you know what I'm saying, rather than me."

Still, he couldn't turn down a once-in-a-lifetime chance, and graciously made the cover. Because he realized it was something bigger than him.

Who has the best helmet in college football? We rank the top 25

Return to Hawaii rejuvenates Jayden Maiava

In May, Maiava returned home to Pālolo. Not to just be back with family, but host a football camp, giving youths that were just like him a chance to learn and experience more about football.

It was a rewarding experience for him, and he saw his younger self in every kid that attended. Just a week before, a storm had wrecked through Oahu, leaving thousands without power and damaged homes. As his cousins, nieces, nephews and other kids went through drills, adults — and even Hawaii Gov. Josh Green — were thanking him for bringing some joy back home.

There was also a pa'ina, a dinner party, with USC alumni on the island for a fundraiser for Hawaiian youth and mental health awareness.

Running back Waymond Jordan joined his quarterback, and he saw how special all of this was for Maiava. He said the trip "meant everything for him" because it's Maiava's community, "so that's like family to me."

All of it reminded Maiava on what he means for culture. It's not lost on him he's the first Polynesian starting quarterback at USC.

"It's unbelievable," he said. "Being that Polynesian player kind of just brings me back to remembering who I am and continuing to stay true to myself.

"It's crazy how everything plays out," he adds, thinking about how not long ago, he was just a kid looking to get out of the house.

Not only a rewarding trip back home, but one that prepared Maiava for 2026. His biggest offseason goals didn't consist of things like throwing the ball quicker, or working on his mobility. What he felt he needed was to focus on the off-the-field things, and work on compartmentalizing everything that comes at him, and nothing like being within your roots to help with that.

"Try to find a quiet in the storm or the quiet in the noise," he said. "Just being present in the moment, putting all my attention to where my feet are at, rather than getting sidetracked with different thoughts and things that go on in my head."

It's a good thing to do, especially considering how loud the noise will be for USC. The pressure is on for Riley and the Trojans to live up to the lofty expectations and make the CFP for the first time. The path isn't be easy, with games against No. 1 Ohio State, No. 2 Oregon and No. 19 Washington, as well as trips to defending champion No. 6 Indiana and No. 17 Penn State in one of the toughest schedules in the country .

No doubt a gauntlet, but if USC is able to regain its spot among college football's elite, it will be because of Maiava's play.

How Jayden Maiava is 'just in a different place'

Several teammates and coaches have touted Maiava's leadership. Offensive lineman Tobias Raymond noted it's easy to tell "how doing it for a while" has helped Maiava get more comfortable.

Usually soft-spoken, he's been noticeably more vocal, and Riley says his quarterback is "bursting with confidence, and just in a different place than he's ever been."

"He's always had some fire about him. He just doesn't always show it in the most outward moments," Riley said. "I think our guys have enjoyed seeing his personality kind of get out there a little bit more and becoming more comfortable.

"It's been fun to see him come out of his shell and show more personality and lead and also do it with kind of the humble nature that kind of really defines who he is."

Maiava credits his experience for paving the way for him to command the team. He will be the second quarterback Riley has had start for three seasons, joining Williams.

Yet, Maiava is far different from the several heralded guys Riley had behind center. You think of names like Williams, Kyler Murray , Jalen Hurts and Baker Mayfield . Maiava is one of a kind in his coach's eyes, and maybe that's why he's not just excited for the potential of his team, but also for the guy that powered his way to get to this spot.

"I get every indication and feeling that he's ready to just play his tail off this year, and he's got a good group of guys around him, and he knows it," Riley said. "His progression has been different than some of the others I've had, just because of where he started and how much he's grown. But I'm super proud of him, and I cannot wait to watch him play this year."

All of it indicates Maiava is out to be one of the best quarterbacks in the country. With the status that comes with USC, he admits the noise can be loud. "Sometimes louder than I would want it," he adds.

The pressure will rise and the occasion must be met. How does he not only survive, but thrive in it? By remembering who he is, and the humble beginnings that brought him to this moment.

"The biggest thing for me is stay true to who I am, and I know who I am," he said.

When talking about the video game cover, he gets reminded other USC cover boys were Heisman Trophy winners — and can't fathom the thought of being on the same level.

" Reggie Bush , Carson Palmer. I mean, Heisman winner guys," Maiava said. "I was just No. 14 up there."

If he has the season he and so many others envision, he won't just be No. 14. He could be the Heisman Trophy-winning No. 14, quarterback of the playoff bound USC Trojans .

Who has the best helmet in college football? Here's a look at the 25 best the sport has to offer heading into the 2026 season. (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch)

NO. 25 OKLAHOMA . Oklahoma's interlocking "OU" is synonymous with one of the most successful programs in college football history, a logo worn by the likes of Billy Sims, Lee Roy Selmon, Brian Bosworth and, more recently, Adrian Peterson and Baker Mayfield. When paired with a shiny crimson helmet, it's one of the best looks in the sport. (Kyle Ross, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 24 ALABAMA . A look synonymous with college football, Alabama has a simple yet beautifully done design with player numbers. Adorning Alabama helmets since the 1950s, the Crimson Tide haven't changed their look much since then, and don't need to. It makes every player stand out while not messing with tradition. A major flex is using the helmet as a logo and the number representing the total national championships, which is at 18 claimed titles. Some teams have done their own versions of adding player numbers to helmets, but it's a design you always associate with the Crimson Tide. (Jeff Hanisch, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 23 WYOMING . The flagship university in the Cowboy State, fittingly, has a cowboy as its mascot and with it, an incredible, distinct logo — a silhouette of a cowboy riding a bucking horse. The image, Bucking Horse and Rider, is actually a registered trademark of the state of Wyoming. The university says it represents "the toughness, and the never-say-die spirit that is Wyoming" and, just as important, it looks awfully good on a helmet. (Troy Babbitt, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 22 BOISE STATE . The non-Power darling does a great job of using a great logo with an oversized look of the Bronco. Oversized logos on helmets usually look good, but this one stands out with how intense it is, especially how Boise State does a nice touch of really making the eye stand out. It could use it on both sides, but it still comes across perfectly on one. No matter what color the helmet or decal is, it works every single time. It's intense and fierce, matching the tenacity that comes with the blue turf. (Mark J. Rebilas, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 21 WASHINGTON STATE . Wazzu has one of the best logos in college sports, a cougar head created by Randall Johnson in 1936 that spells out the school's initials, "WSU." It has become an iconic symbol for the university and in the broader college football world, thanks in some part to Ol' Crimson, a Washington State flag that has been in the background of every episode of "College GameDay" since 2003. (Petre Thomas, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 20 NEBRASKA . The Cornhuskers became a powerhouse when it added the block "N," and while there's nothing special about it, the helmet still is among the most recognizable. Nebraska has tried different variations with black that have mostly looked decent, but it further proves there is no need to mess with good ol' reliable. (Jeff Hanisch, IMAGN IMAGES)

articles.title: Why United might not be done in the transfer window just yet
articles.summary: Apart from replacing backup goalkeeper Altay Bayındır with Karl Darlow on a free transfer, Manchester United’s sole transfer business this summer has come in...
articles.body:
Apart from replacing backup goalkeeper Altay Bayındır with Karl Darlow on a free transfer, Manchester United 's sole transfer business this summer has come in midfield. They've spent north of €170m on Carlos Baleba , Andrey Santos , and Youri Tielemans in order to replace Casemiro , who has joined Inter Miami on a free transfer, and Manuel Ugarte , who injured his knee ligament in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. They've also freed up their wage bill with the departures of Jadon Sancho , Tyrell Malacia and Rasmus Højlund, in addition to selling youth products Radek Vítek and Tyler Fredricson . And with less than a week left in the summer transfer window, they might not be done yet.

Manchester United look poised to add a left back to their ranks before Tuesday's deadline and reinforce a position that has been weakened (albeit not dramatically) by Malacia's exit. Apart from Luke Shaw , United don't have a single natural left back, and whilst the likes of Diogo Dalot , Noussair Mazraoui , Patrick Dorgu , and Lisandro Martínez have been used there in the past, it's clear that they're far more comfortable elsewhere in the backline. And despite being used as Shaw's backup in preseason, Harry Amass was not included in United's matchday squad in their opening-day defeat to Hull City.

Relying on a 31-year-old Shaw to stay fit for the entirety of the campaign is a risky bet, especially considering that he's missed 103 matches with injury since the start of the 2023/24 season. It's undeniable that United need to sign a left back – the only question is, who? United's main priority in the window would have undoubtedly been Lewis Hall ; Newcastle will demand a king's ransom after already losing two of their biggest assets in Bruno Guimarães and Anthony Gordon .

RB Leipzig , meanwhile, will be reticent to lose yet another key figure after selling Yan Diomande for a club-record €125 million, and will be looking to keep hold of David Raum . The German is entering the final year of his contract, but he could cost a pretty penny at £30m, less than half of what Newcastle are reportedly demanding for Hall.

There are other options like Jorge Salinas, 19, who has spurred Racing Santander to promotion but seems to be more of a natural center back rather than a fullback. Whilst Salinas has a £13.6 million release clause in his contract, it remains to be seen whether he can make the jump from the Segunda to the Premier League.

Another name that has been mentioned is Myles Lewis-Skelly , with Arsenal holding out for a fee in the region of £50 million. Lewis-Skelly enjoyed a fine end to the season, helping the Gunners win their first Premier League title in two decades and earning praise from the likes of Steve Fletcher . But after playing himself back into Mikel Arteta's starting XI, it seems unlikely that Arsenal would sanction a move so late in the window.

Last but not least, United could be tempted to sign Alejandro Balde from FC Barcelona . Once considered the present and future of Barcelona's left back position, Balde has been decimated by injuries and inconsistent form, prompting him to be leapfrogged in Hansi Flick's hierarchy by João Cancelo , with young talents like Gerard Martin and Xavi Espart waiting in the wings. He wasn't part of the matchday squad in the season opener, which saw Barcelona thrash Elche 5-0, with Flick stating, "I need everyone to be 100 per cent committed to us."

It remains to be seen who they end up going for, but one thing's clear: United need to give Michael Carrick a new left back in order for them to maximize their potential this season.

articles.title: Column: As pressure builds, Mike Norvell keeps retreating further into his shell of reduced access
articles.summary: FSU has gone from one of the most open programs in media access to one of the more restricted.
articles.body:
As Mike Norvell enters what is expected to be a make-or-break season leading the Florida State football program, he's outwardly projected an air of confidence about his team.

He's talked highly of the returning players, the new additions and lessons learned from last two years' struggles that will ensure things go better this fall.

His actions, though, tell another story. It's not that long ago that Norvell's program was as open in terms of media access as any in college football. Writers who covered Florida State were allowed to watch the majority of the spring and preseason practices in their entirety and watched three full practices a week for the first five seasons of Norvell's tenure.

That went away ahead of the 2025 season, with FSU now among the least accessible programs in terms of practice viewing access.

That, in itself, was a questionable decision. After all, we were there throughout Norvell's initial build, including the 13-0 season, and were there three times a week for the 2-10 2024 season.

So the intimation that media access had anything to do with results on the field is not based on any real evidence.

Now, Norvell is taking the idea of letting out as little information as possible to an even more extreme level this season, announcing Monday that FSU will not release any depth charts in 2026.

While some college football programs have begun not releasing depth charts until the first game in an attempt to hide as many details as possible, it's certainly not anything close to the norm for teams to outright refuse to release depth charts.

Talking Monday about his decision, Norvell indicated it's being made due to the players rather than due to outside perceptions.

"Right now, guys know where they are. Every player wants more. That's what it should be," he said. "You should want to be the starter. You should want to be the guy that plays the most plays. … But also, on the flip side of it, if we come out with a depth chart today that says, well, this is what it looks like. Throughout the course of the week, there's ups, downs, whatever that might be. Somebody puts themselves in position, well, the best players are going to play.

"Just, go have a great week. Whatever personnel groupings, if you're a starter in, then you're a starter. If you're not, then continue to work and get better and put yourself in that position."

Considering the players certainly have a rough idea of the pecking order on the depth chart from being involved in preseason camp — even if it's no longer being shared publicly — it's hard to take this as the real reason.

It's not nearly as big a deal as the other two, but FSU also elected to make Inside Seminole Football a studio show this season, removing the in-person audience, and Monday's first edition of the season had an audio delay.

Meanwhile, second-year men's basketball coach Luke Loucks has taken over Norvell's former crown of the media-friendly coach in Tallahassee, with practice availability basically whenever a media member wants to go and transparent messaging.

Norvell returned the Seminoles to their former glory, albeit for just a brief spell, on the basis of transparency and that it was not a necessary competitive advantage to conform to the restricted access pretty much all of the rest of college football coaches utilized. He proved that thought process correct during a 19-game win streak spanning the 2022 and '23 seasons.

But now, as the walls continue to close in more and more, that tune has changed. It's hard not to feel like Norvell now believes he needs every smidge of competitive advantage he can manage by limiting intel.

Norvell's words are saying one thing. But his actions are saying quite another.

articles.title: When is the UEFA Champions League draw? What to know about format
articles.summary: The 2026-27 UEFA Champions League draw for the league phase of the tournament will be held on Thursday, Aug. 27 in Monaco.
articles.body:
The qualifying rounds for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League are complete and now it's time to look forward to the league phase of Europe's annual premier club tournament.

Paris Saint-Germain enters this year's competition as two-time reigning champions, and looking to become the first three-peat Champions League winner since Real Madrid from 2016-18.

Count 15-time Champions League winners Real Madrid among the biggest threats to PSG's throne, a list of contenders that also includes (but is not exclusive to) defending Premier League winners Arsenal , Bundesliga champs Bayern Munich and La Liga title-holders FC Barcelona .

The UEFA Champions League enters the third season under its relatively new format, with 36 teams in one "league" and each club playing eight matches. The top eight teams advance to the round of 16, while the 9th-24th-placed finishers play a two-legged tie to get into the knockout round proper.

Here's what to know about Thursday's draw:

Ranking Premier League stadiums from biggest to smallest

How does the Champions League draw work?

Thirty-six European clubs will participate in the league phase, with each being assigned eight opponents – four home matches and four on the road – in Thursday's draw.

The clubs enter the draw in four pots based on UEFA rankings and cannot be matched up against another team from their own country (ex: Arsenal can't draw Manchester City ), and no team can face more than two opponents from any other country.

The 36 clubs all play in one "league" with matches staged on select Tuesdays and Wednesdays through January, with the top eight teams advancing directly to the round of 16.

The teams that finish ninth-24th enter the knockout round playoffs in February, two legged ties that will determine the other eight teams in the last 16.

Once the 16 remaining teams are determined, the rest of the bracket is drawn – with the top eight finishers seeded.

Pot 1: Arsenal, Manchester City, Bayern Munich , Paris Saint-Germain , Liverpool , Inter Milan , Real Madrid, FC Barcelona , Atlético Madrid

Pot 2: Aston Villa , Sporting CP, FC Porto, Borussia Dortmund , AS Roma , Manchester United , Club Brugge, Real Betis , PSV Eindhoven

articles.title: Jackson deal expected to trigger Watkins exit
articles.summary: If Senegal international Nicolas Jackson agrees personal terms and completes the switch to Aston Villa from Chelsea, his arrival is expected to trigger Ollie...
articles.body:
If Senegal international Nicolas Jackson agrees personal terms and completes the switch to Aston Villa from Chelsea , his arrival is expected to trigger Ollie Watkins ' move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

A deal worth about £51m will see the 30-year-old leave Villa Park, having joined the club from Brentford in 2020 and become their record Premier League goalscorer with 108 top-flight goals.

Villa had been preparing to sell Watkins, but they needed to replace him before sanctioning a move. He missed Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Brighton , with boss Unai Emery saying it was up to him and his agent to explain why.

The Jackson move remains subject to personal terms being agreed but negotiations are at an advanced stage, with Jackson expected to reunite with Emery having played under him at Villarreal .

He would become the latest player in Villa's summer rebuild, following the arrivals of record-buy Johan Manzambi , midfielder Joao Gomes , goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and defender Matteo Ruggeri .

However, there has also been significant movement out of the club and Watkins leaving would mean they have sold five of the starting XI who won the Europa League in May.

articles.title: Bayern's Kompany: Musiala back soon, Karl returns to squad
articles.summary: Jamal Musiala is closing in on a return to action for Bayern Munich but will not be available for the Bundesliga season opener against VfB Stuttgart on Frida...
articles.body:
Jamal Musiala is closing in on a return to action for Bayern Munich but will not be available for the Bundesliga season opener against VfB Stuttgart on Friday, coach Vincent Kompany said.

The 23-year-old collapsed due to absence seizures in two pre-season friendlies and is sitting out the start to the campaign while his medication is adjusted.

"Basically Jamal is doing relatively well," Kompany told a news conference on Thursday, adding that Musiala was set to take full part in Bayern's final training session. "But he will not yet be in the squad."

Musiala is still getting used "to the increase in medication." A decision on a match comeback would be made "hand in hand with the experts," Kompany said.

Winger Lennart Karl will be back in the Bayern squad for the first time since his muscle injury before the World Cup, having missed the 2-1 win against Borussia Dortmund in the Franz Beckenbauer Super Cup last Saturday alongside Musiala.

"How big his role can be, we will have to wait and see," Kompany said of Karl, 18.

Kompany is heading into his third Bayern season and has positive feelings as he seeks a third straight Bundesliga title.

"I always have the belief in my head that we can be successful in the end. But you are never sure and that also gives you impetus. In my head I have zero titles, I have to show everything again," he added.

In the final match of last season, Bayern beat Stuttgart 3-0 in the German Cup final in Berlin with three goals from Harry Kane .

Last season, the record champions opened the Bundesliga with an emphatic 6-0 victory at the Allianz Arena against RB Leipzig .

articles.title: "¿Farmear aura?": la 'broma' viral que le costó la 'nevera' a un árbitro argentino
articles.standfirst: El uso de tal expresión le ha costado al colegiado Fernando Espinoza no ser incluido en ninguna terna arbitral para la séptima fecha del Torneo Clausura por parte de la Dirección Nacional de Arbitraje
articles.summary: El uso de tal expresión le ha costado al colegiado Fernando Espinoza no ser incluido en ninguna terna arbitral para la séptima fecha del Torneo Clausura por parte de la Dirección Nacional de Arbitraje
articles.body: Un gesto pensado para romper el hielo terminó convirtiéndose en un problema serio para el arbitraje argentino. Fernando Espinoza, colegiado de Primera División, protagonizó el pasado domingo uno de los momentos más comentados de la sexta fecha del Torneo Clausura durante el sorteo previo al partido entre Belgrano y Defensa y Justicia, disputado en el estadio Julio César Villagra de Córdoba. Ante los capitanes Lisandro López y Leandro Fernández, y utilizando una moneda personalizada con los escudos de ambos clubes, Espinoza lanzó una pregunta insólita para ese momento tan formal del protocolo: si querían hacer una "competencia de farmear aura", expresión surgida de la jerga de internet y los videojuegos que hace referencia a acumular carisma o presencia mediante gestos y poses. Los jugadores no aceptaron la propuesta y el sorteo continuó con normalidad, con López quedándose finalmente con la moneda tras ganarlo. El vídeo del momento se viralizó rápidamente en redes sociales, e incluso los propios relatores de ESPN Premium llegaron a calificarlo como "el mejor sorteo del campeonato". Sin embargo, la reacción en las oficinas de la Dirección Nacional de Arbitraje (DNA), que dirige Federico Beligoy, fue radicalmente distinta. Días antes del partido, la DNA ya había enviado una circular a todos los colegiados fijando pautas estrictas para la ceremonia del sorteo, prohibiendo de forma expresa cualquier expresión, comentario o manifestación ajena al procedimiento, que debía realizarse con la seriedad y formalidad correspondientes.

articles.title: Abde y Morante apuran sus opciones de estar el sábado frente al Levante
articles.standfirst: Suman este jueves una sesión más de entrenamiento con sus compañeros
articles.summary: Suman este jueves una sesión más de entrenamiento con sus compañeros
articles.body: Abde y Morante son las dos principales dudas del Betis de cara al partido que el equipo de Pellegrini disputará este próximo sábado en el Estadio Ciudad de Valencia frente al Levante, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de Liga. Ambos han sumado este jueves una sesión más de entrenamiento con el grupo y será el cuerpo técnico, de acuerdo con los servicios médicos verdiblancos, quien decida mañana si están ya en disposición de viajar con el equipo y tener minutos. El extremo marroquí se lesionó el pasado mes de junio en el último amistoso de su selección previo al Mundial, en el que terminó siendo baja. Desde entonces no ha podido volver a jugar, aunque hace ya varios días que se ejercita con sus compañeros avanzando en su puesta a punto tras superar el problema de rodilla que sufrió en aquel encuentro ante Noruega. El canterano, por su parte, se perdió los dos primeros partidos de Liga por unas molestias, pero desde el pasado domingo trabaja ya con aparente normalidad con el equipo. El resto del equipo, a excepción de los lesionados Diego Conde, Aitor Ruibal, Giovani Lo Celso y Gonzalo Petit, está disponible para el fin de semana, a la espera de posibles movimientos de mercado. Esta mañana se oficializó la marcha de Gnangoro Bouare al Rayo Vallecano y jugadores como Iker Losada o el propio Petit están en la rampa de salida. El Betis busca plusvalías con las que poder afrontar alguna incorporación más de aquí al cierre del mercado del próximo martes. A nivel deportivo, después de sumar de tres en tres tanto en el partido de La Cartuja ante la Real Sociedad como el martes en Mestalla frente al Valencia, los de Pellegrini buscan seguir con su pleno para intentar asaltar el liderato de la clasificación. En estos momentos están empatados con seis puntos con Real Madrid y Sevilla, pero ocupan la tercera posición de la tabla por la diferencia de goles y el número de goles marcados.

articles.title: Oficial: Livakovic firma por el Barça
articles.standfirst: El veterano meta croata refuerza la meta culé hasta junio de 2030
articles.summary: El veterano meta croata refuerza la meta culé hasta junio de 2030
articles.body: Dominik Livakovic ya es jugador del Barcelona. El veterano meta croata pasó en las últimas horas la revisión médica y el Barça confirmó hoy su incorporación. Firma por cuatro temporadas y la operación con el Fenerbahce se cerró en dos millones de euros fijos más medio en variables. El jugador ficha hasta junio de 2030. El club catalán oficializó esta jornada el fichaje de Dominik Livakovic, portero croata de 31 años. El cancerbero, que llegó ayer a Barcelona, procede del Fenerbahce, entidad con la que tenía contrato hasta junio de 2028. Refuerza la meta de Flick, que cuenta con Joan García y Szczesny. Ter Stegen, que no contaba para Flick, se marchó cedido al Ajax de Míchel. El arquero internacional tiene una dilatada trayectoria. Disputó, por ejemplo, 310 encuentros con el Dinamo de Zagreb, 108 con el NK Zagreb, 74 con el Fenerbahce... además militó en la filas del Girona, estuvo cedido unos meses en la campaña 25-26, aunque no intervino en ningún encuentro con el equipo de Montilivi. La intención del Barcelona es que Livakovic sea el segundo portero de Hansi Flick. El primero es Joan García, pero el internacional croata, que suma 79 partidos con su combinado nacional, adelantaría, por lo tanto, como primer suplente a Szczesny. El club catalán está pendiente, no obstante, de saber exactamente su situación con el fair-play para confirmar su presencia en el banquillo culé, ya que si no puede encajar su ficha se irá cedido a otra entidad. La llegada del internacional provoca que Eder Aller e Iker Rodríguez, si se confirma que Livakovic se queda en el Spotify Camp Nou, vayan a tener menos protagonismo en el primer equipo azulgrana.

articles.title: Liam Delap joins Nottingham Forest in club-record £50m deal as Chelsea make profit on striker
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest sign Liam Delap in club-record £50m deal from Chelsea; striker  moved to Stamford Bridge last summer from Ipswich Town but scored just two goals in 41 games; Chelsea could make a profit of up to £20m having signed the 23-year-old for £30m
articles.body:
The transfer is understood to be worth at least £45m, potentially reaching £50m with add-ons, meaning Chelsea could make up to £20m profit on the 23-year-old, having only signed him from Ipswich Town last summer for £30m.

The forward has signed a five-year deal at the City Ground. "I really can't wait to get started. This is a massive club with a big history," he said in a statement.

"I spoke to the manager and I like his way. I think he can be the one to really help me develop and make that next step and hopefully I can bring goals here."

Delap made 47 appearances for Chelsea, scoring just three times, after impressing for Ipswich, where he netted 12 Premier League goals in 37 games as they were relegated from the top flight in 2024/25.

Delap had interest from several other Premier League clubs, including Everton.

Forest's previous record transfer saw Omari Hutchison join for £37.5m from Ipswich Town in August 2025.

How have Chelsea made a profit on Delap?

From a business perspective, this represents a superb sale for Chelsea as they bank a huge profit on a player who scored just three times in an underwhelming campaign at Stamford Bridge.

Many outsiders baulked at the £50m price tag which Chelsea slapped on Delap's head this summer but the Blues are set to receive the full asking price if the add-ons attached to the deal are achieved.

Chelsea capitalised on a market opportunity last summer. Delap's £30m release clause following Ipswich's relegation had many leading Premier League clubs interested. The forward scored 12 goals in the Tractor Boys' 2024/25 season in the top flight.

And a forgettable campaign in west London has not put off Nottingham Forest. A dearth of proven, natural No 9s means they come at a premium.

Forest's need is pretty clear too. Oliver Glasner doesn't like to be pigeonholed tactically, but his main success as a manager has come when he's had a focal point up front, whether that be Jean-Philippe Mateta, Randal Kolo Muani or Wout Weghorst.

Chris Wood has enjoyed a resurgence in his 30s but struggled with injuries last season. Igor Jesus has impressed at the City Ground but isn't necessarily suited to a target-man role. With Taiwo Awoniyi sold on, Arnaud Kalimuendo represents the only other option. Short in stature, the French forward would not appear a natural fit the job that Glasner will assign.

It's an expensive deal and comes with risk. The last 12 months has been an ordeal for Delap and his confidence has taken a huge knock. But the remarkable role Glasner played in galvanising Mateta and turning him into a leading Premier League striker and French international should give everybody belief that the 23-year-old can get his career back on track.

Forest have brought in Delap to improve their striking options following Taiwo Awoniyi's £9m move to Coventry City.

Glasner's side have been pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall as an Elliot Anderson replacement, but Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi insists he is staying in north London.

Forest could also add a right wing-back, with Fiorentina's Dodo a player of interest.

Winger Dilane Bakwa is set to join Lille on loan while defender Eric da Silva Moreira has joined Eredivisie club Excelsior on a temporary deal. Centre-backs Zach Abbott and Tyler Bindon could also depart on loan amid interest from Watford.

articles.title: Cole Palmer: Chelsea attacker ready to put troublesome 2025/26 season behind him after promising start under Xabi Alonso
articles.summary: Cole Palmer impressed during Xabi Alonso's first Premier League win as Chelsea boss against Fulham; Palmer revealed the 'freedom' he feels playing under the Spaniard; watch Chelsea vs Luton live in Carabao Cup action from 7.15pm on Thursday, kick-off 7.30pm
articles.body:
The 24-year-old endured a difficult 2025-26 season, picking up a groin issue which saw him play just twice between August and December.

And while he ended up with 10 Premier League goals, a run of one goal in eight games to end the campaign saw him miss out on England's World Cup squad.

Palmer put that disappointment behind him on Monday as he got off the mark in the Blues' opener against Fulham en route to a 3-2 win. His performance was a reminder of his star quality.

"Physically I feel good, probably the best I've felt in ages, but I think I can [get fitter] with games and more minutes," Palmer told Sky Sports .

"Before my groin injury, I'd never really been injured. Well, rarely [injured]. So then I would just come back and play when I shouldn't have played.

"Obviously the World Cup was coming up, so I was in a bit of a dilemma thinking: 'if I don't play I'm not going to go. But if I play then, I can't play [properly]'.

"It was just a bit of a sticky situation. I didn't really know how to deal with it, but it's one of those things. I was just seeing different people, getting different ideas of why I was injured and what it was.

"Since I've come back I've been working every day to obviously stop it happening again. I just want to stay injury free, and if I'm on the pitch then I know what I can do."

Alonso giving Palmer the keys to freedom

While it is early days, Palmer appears to have been given the license to express himself once again under Alonso.

At times during the tenures of Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior, suggestions were made that Palmer was being shackled as a result of more rigid systems. He even alluded to that himself, but revealed it was no longer the case following conversations with his new boss.

"He [Alonso] just said I'd have more freedom to drift about the pitch. Just like you saw [against Fulham] with the goal I scored.

"Last season, I wouldn't have even made that run because it's not a 'safe zone'. But he's saying move across that zone, drop into play, come get on the ball, create and just do what you do."

That new sense of freedom could help forge lethal attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and new signing Morgan Rogers . All three scored at Craven Cottage and have since been dubbed 'JP Morgan.'

While Palmer is absolutely not a fan of the name, he is excited by the budding relationship between the trio.

"It's a rubbish name. We need to come up with something better than that," he joked. "I think we've got a different mix of qualities. Joao can do a bit of everything. Morgan's more physical and I'm more technical, so I think we've got a good balance."

The win over Fulham gave Chelsea the perfect start, and with Alonso's expertise and no European football, some have tipped the Blues to become surprise title contenders.

Speaking on Monday Night Football , Gary Neville did suggest that the strength of Arsenal could be too much to overcome. However, he felt that Chelsea were in a good place and backed them to make a push for second place.

Regardless, Palmer revealed that no discussion had taken place within the dressing room regarding the table.

"We've not even spoken about it," Palmer said. "You can't say title race yet, we've only played one game."

However, when asked if he believed the quality was in the squad to challenge, Palmer responded: "Yeah, I think so."

articles.title: Allan Elias to Man City: How Brazilian overcame tragedy to go from 'Mini Balotelli' to Palmeiras' underrated gem
articles.summary: With Manchester City signing Allan Elias from Palmeiras, Adam Bate examines the Brazilian late bloomer's tragic but inspiring backstory with insight from the former coach who is backing him to become a success in the Premier League under Enzo Maresca...
articles.body:
They should not be concerned. Allan's £34m move from Palmeiras to the Premier League looks a smart signing by City, a talented and versatile player ready to contribute. With Allan, it is more a case of work ethic than wonderkid as wingers go. And his story is inspiring.

Allan's beginnings are not just humble but tragic. The death of his old Figueirense teammate Vitor Isaias in a fire at Flamengo's academy accommodation in 2019 that killed 10 people had a profound effect. His family moved to Sao Paulo to be near him.

During the pandemic, Allan's sister Leticia died due to Covid-19. The 'L' gesture made with his hands after scoring is in her honour. There is the tattoo of best friend Gustavo Paco, who died in a motorcycle accident the day after the pair had played on the beach.

It is a life blighted by misfortune but also its own little miracle. This football success was not supposed to happen for Allan. He felt close to leaving Palmeiras for very different reasons as recently as late 2024, having seen so many others promoted ahead of him.

He cried with his parents before his final U20 game, thinking it was all over. Approaching 21 and seemingly overlooked by his own club, coach Abel Ferreira then pulled him aside in training to let him know that he would be getting a new contract.

The rest is history. Allan emerged as a key player for Palmeiras over the past 18 months, no teenage prodigy but an underrated gem. "Allan is a different player," his former coach Lucas Andrade tells Sky Sports . "He needed more time, but now he is at the same level."

Andrade was Allan's coach at U15 and U20 level at Palmeiras. "He scored a lot of goals." But it was at a youth tournament in England of all places that he became convinced. "That is when I realised Allan had the level to play here one day," he says.

"He played very well against Chelsea, against Tottenham. The final was Manchester City against Chelsea. And I watched the game with Allan in the crowd. And now, many years later, he has come back to England to play for Manchester City. It is a very nice story."

His youth coach might have believed but others had not seen it. Those tears before his final U20 appearance were because Allan did not know what was coming next. But Ferreira spotted something and told the sporting director that he must stay.

He made his senior debut in January of last year, scoring his first goal the next month. His parents went viral in Brazil after filming their joyful celebrations. By the summer, Allan was a starter at the Club World Cup in what had been Estevao's right-wing spot.

Palmeiras reached the quarter-finals, with Estevao, on the eve of his big move to Chelsea, playing in a more advanced role while Allan did the dirty work on the wing. It reflected the trust of the coach, a recognition that he can do both sides of the game.

That was Ferreira's explanation for the interest in Allan with the City transfer imminent. "Teams want players like Allan because he does what 90 per cent of the wingers here cannot do," he explained. "Attack and defend down the flank for the full 90 minutes."

It is why the statistics do not necessarily do Allan justice. In this season's Brazilian championship, for example, he has four goals and three assists in 21 appearances. There are more compelling highlights compilations around but he has his moments.

Most notably, he set up the first goal and won the penalty for the last one in the second leg of the Copa Libertadores semi-final against Liga de Quito last year. Palmeiras won the game 4-0 to turn around a three-goal deficit from the tie in the altitude of Ecuador.

One of his more famous goals for Palmeiras came against Flamengo when he put his head in where it hurt to score in a 3-0 win in May. Former Manchester United player Guillermo Varela was threatening to take his block off with an ill-judged scissor-kick.

Now 22, there is grit to his game but he is a dribbler as well, currently ranking second in the Brazilian top flight for successful take-ons this season. He is particularly fond of that chop inside onto his stronger left foot. "He is very good one-vs-one," says Andrade.

Superficially, there are some similarities with Savio, the compatriot he is replacing at City. Andrade has worked with both. "They are similar in some ways. Both are very good dribblers. But I think Allan is more strong and Savio is more technical," he reveals.

But Allan's greatest asset is less obvious than strength or technique. It is the resilience that he has had to show in life and the adaptability that he has shown on the pitch. "I think he is a tactical player," says Andrade. "Technical, but he is a tactical player too."

For Palmeiras, he has been the joker in the pack. "Allan can play in the middle, can play in both sides of attack. Helps a lot in defence. In the academy, he played more times in the middle. But in the first team, he plays on the side, especially on the right side."

More recently, his versatility has been evident with him filling in on the right of Ferreira's 3-4-1-2 formation. Allan is essentially an attacking right wing-back, cutting inside on his left foot. It is a demanding role that requires as much without the ball as with it.

"I think this characteristic is so important in the Premier League. Being just technical today is not possible." Particularly under Enzo Maresca. "With Maresca, I think the players change. Play inside, play outside. It is a characteristic of Allan, his versatility."

It is an interesting observation. Maresca is regarded as a disciple of Pep Guardiola, an advocate of positional play. But this ability to switch positions is also a feature of his tactics. "The important thing for me in the Maresca style is mobility," argues Andrade.

"I think Allan is a perfect player for this because he plays on both sides and in the middle. Savio has a position where he normally just plays on the right side and has a great capacity here. But I think the other option with this coach is important."

From Mini Balotelli to major Brazilian signing, there is confidence that he is ready for this. "I believe he can make a good impact in the Premier League." But that is perhaps the smaller story given all that Allan has overcome. The triumph is just making it here.
